title.zh: 卷五十 志第三十: 刑法
title.raw: 卷五十 志第三十: 刑法 Volume 50 Treatises 30: Punishment and Law

sentences.zh: 志第三十刑法

translations.literal: Treatise 30: Punishment and Law
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 30: Punishment and Law

sentences.zh: 古之聖人，為人父母，莫不制禮以崇敬，立刑以明威，防閑于未然，懼爭心之將作也。

translations.literal: The ancient sages, in their role as parents of the people, all without exception established ritual to foster reverence and set up punishments to display authority, guarding against misconduct before it arose, fearing that contentious hearts were about to stir.
translations.idiomatic: The sages of antiquity, acting as parents to the people, invariably established ritual to inspire reverence and instituted punishments to make authority manifest. They sought to forestall wrongdoing before it could take shape, dreading the rise of contentious hearts.

sentences.zh: 故有輕重三典之異，宮墨五刑之差，度時而施宜，因事以議制。

translations.literal: Therefore there were distinctions among the three statutes of varying severity, and differences among the five punishments of mutilation and tattooing; they gauged the times and applied what was fitting, devising regulations in accordance with affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hence arose the varying grades of the three great codes and the gradations of the five bodily punishments—mutilation, branding, and the rest—applied as the times required and shaped to the matter at hand.

sentences.zh: 大則陳之原野，小則肆諸市朝，以禦奸宄，用懲禍亂。

translations.literal: For grave cases they were exposed in the open countryside; for lesser ones they were displayed in the market and court, to repel traitors and rebels and to punish calamity and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Grave offenders were executed in the open country; lesser ones were put to death in the marketplace and at court—all to ward off treachery and insurrection and to chasten disaster and rebellion.

sentences.zh: 興邦致理，罔有弗由於此者也。

translations.literal: Raising a state and bringing order to rule—nothing fails to proceed from this.
translations.idiomatic: No state has ever been raised to glory or brought to good governance without recourse to such measures.

sentences.zh: 暨淳樸既消，澆偽斯起，刑增為九，章積三千，雖有凝脂次骨之峻，而錐刀之末，盡爭之矣。

translations.literal: When simple honesty had vanished and shallow falsity arose, punishments were increased to nine, and statutes accumulated to three thousand; though there were the severity of congealed fat and crushed bone, yet at the tip of an awl or knife all strove over them.
translations.idiomatic: Once innocent simplicity faded and corrupt artifice took hold, punishments multiplied to nine degrees and statutes piled up to three thousand clauses. Even when penalties were as harsh as congealed grease and pulverized bone, people still wrangled over the smallest legal niceties.

sentences.zh: 自漢迄隋，世有增損，而罕能折衷。

translations.literal: From Han through Sui, each age had additions and reductions, yet few were able to strike a mean.
translations.idiomatic: From the Han through the Sui, successive dynasties revised the code, yet few managed to strike a balanced middle path.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝參用周、齊舊政，以定律令，除苛慘之法，務在寬平。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui drew upon the old policies of Zhou and Qi to fix statutes and ordinances, abolishing harsh and cruel laws, striving for lenience and even-handedness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui adopted elements of the Zhou and Northern Qi legal systems to draft his statutes, repealing cruel and oppressive laws in favor of leniency and fairness.

sentences.zh: 比及晚年，漸亦滋虐。

translations.literal: By the time of his later years, he gradually became more oppressive as well.
translations.idiomatic: By his later years, however, his rule grew increasingly harsh.

sentences.zh: 煬帝忌刻，法令尤峻，人不堪命，遂至於亡。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang was suspicious and harsh; his laws and ordinances were especially severe; people could not bear their lot, and at last [the dynasty] perished.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang was mistrustful and vindictive; his laws were extraordinarily severe. The people could no longer endure their lot, and the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 高祖初起義師於太原，即布寬大之令。

translations.literal: When Gaozu first raised his righteous army at Taiyuan, he immediately promulgated lenient and generous orders.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu first raised his army of righteousness at Taiyuan, he immediately issued orders of clemency and leniency.

sentences.zh: 百姓苦隋苛政，競來歸附。

translations.literal: The common people, suffering under the harsh government of Sui, all hastened to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The people, ground down by the Sui's harsh rule, flocked to join him.

sentences.zh: 旬月之間，遂成帝業。

translations.literal: Within a month or so, he thus accomplished his imperial enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Within a matter of weeks he had secured the throne.

sentences.zh: 既平京城，約法為十二條。

translations.literal: Once he had pacified the capital region, he compacted the law into twelve articles.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying the capital, he promulgated a provisional code of twelve articles.

sentences.zh: 惟制殺人、劫盜、背軍、叛逆者死，餘並蠲除之。

translations.literal: He prescribed death only for murderers, robbers, deserters, and rebels, and abolished all the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Only murder, robbery, desertion, and treason were made capital offenses; all other punishments were abolished.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，詔納言劉文靜與當朝通識之士，因開皇律令而損益之，盡削大業所用煩峻之法。

translations.literal: Upon receiving the abdication, he ordered the Counselor-in-chief Liu Wenjing together with knowledgeable men of the court to take the Kaihuang statutes and ordinances and revise them by additions and subtractions, entirely cutting away the cumbersome and severe laws used in the Daye reign.
translations.idiomatic: After taking the throne, he commanded Counselor-in-Chief Liu Wenjing and other learned officials of the court to revise the Kaihuang code, eliminating entirely the burdensome and severe laws of the Daye era.

sentences.zh: 又制五十三條格，務在寬簡，取便於時。

translations.literal: He also devised fifty-three supplementary regulations, striving for lenience and simplicity, taking what was convenient for the time.
translations.idiomatic: He also drafted fifty-three supplementary regulations, aiming for simplicity and leniency suited to the needs of the day.

sentences.zh: 尋又敕尚書左僕射裴寂、尚書右僕射蕭瑀及大理卿崔善為、給事中王敬業、中書舍人劉林甫顏師古王孝遠、涇州別駕靖延、太常丞丁孝烏、隋大理丞房軸、上將府參軍李桐客、太常博士徐上機等，撰定律令，大略以開皇為准。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he also ordered Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Pei Ji, Right Vice Director Xiao Yu, and Grand Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Cui Shanwei, Attending Gentleman Wang Jingye, Secretariat Drafters Liu Linfu, Yan Shigu, and Wang Xiaoyuan, Tongzhou Registrar Jing Yan, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Ding Xiaowu, former Sui Grand Judge Fang Zhou, Staff Officer of the General-in-Chief's Office Li Tongke, and Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Xu Shangji and others to compile and fix statutes and ordinances, in the main taking Kaihuang as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: He soon charged Vice Ministers Pei Ji and Xiao Yu, Grand Judge Cui Shanwei, Attending Gentleman Wang Jingye, Secretariat drafters Liu Linfu, Yan Shigu, and Wang Xiaoyuan, Registrar Jing Yan of Tongzhou, Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices Ding Xiaowu, former Sui judge Fang Zhou, staff officer Li Tongke of the generalissimo's headquarters, Erudite Xu Shangji of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and others to compile the statutes, taking the Kaihuang code as their general model.

sentences.zh: 于時諸事始定，邊方尚梗，救時之弊，有所未暇，惟正五十三條格，入於新律，餘無所改。

translations.literal: At that time all affairs had just been settled and the frontier regions were still obstructed; to remedy the ills of the time, there were matters for which he had no leisure, and he only rectified the fifty-three supplementary regulations and incorporated them into the new code, changing nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs were only just settling and the frontiers remained troubled; pressing urgencies left little time for thorough revision. Only the fifty-three supplementary regulations were corrected and incorporated into the new code; nothing else was changed.

sentences.zh: 至武德七年五月奏上，乃下詔曰：

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year of Wude it was submitted; he then issued an edict saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the seventh year of Wude the code was submitted to the throne, and the emperor issued an edict that read:

sentences.zh: 古不云乎，「萬邦之君，有典有則。

translations.literal: Does not antiquity say, "The lord of ten thousand states has statutes and has norms"?
translations.idiomatic: Did not the ancients say, "The ruler of all lands possesses statutes and norms"?

sentences.zh: 」故九疇之敘，興于夏世，兩觀之法，大備隆周。

translations.literal: " Therefore the ordering of the Nine Categories arose in the age of Xia, and the laws of the two audience halls were fully perfected in the flourishing Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Thus the ordering of the Nine Categories arose in the Xia, and the laws of the two audience halls reached their full development in the great Zhou.

sentences.zh: 所以禁暴懲奸，弘風闡化，安民立政，莫此為先。

translations.literal: By this means to restrain violence and punish treachery, to expand custom and unfold transformation, to settle the people and establish government—nothing takes precedence over this.
translations.idiomatic: Through such means violence is restrained, treachery punished, customs elevated, civilization spread, the people secured, and government established—nothing takes precedence over this.

sentences.zh: 自戰國紛擾，恃詐任力，苛制煩刑，於茲競起。

translations.literal: From the time when the Warring States were in turmoil, relying on deceit and trusting in force, harsh regulations and burdensome punishments all arose in rivalry here.
translations.idiomatic: From the turmoil of the Warring States onward, rulers relied on deceit and brute force; harsh regulations and excessive punishments arose in endless succession.

sentences.zh: 秦並天下，隳滅禮教，恣行酷烈，害虐蒸民，宇內騷然，遂以顛覆。

translations.literal: Qin united the realm, destroyed ritual and teaching, and wantonly practiced cruelty and severity, harming and oppressing the teeming masses; within the four seas there was turmoil, and at last [the dynasty] was overthrown.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin united the realm it destroyed ritual and learning, practicing cruelty without restraint and oppressing the people until the empire was in turmoil and the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 漢氏撥亂，思易前軌，雖復務從約法，蠲削嚴刑，尚行菹醢之誅，猶設錙銖之禁。

translations.literal: The house of Han quelled disorder and sought to change the former course; though again they strove to follow simplified law and abolished severe punishments, they still practiced the punishment of mincing and still set prohibitions as fine as a zhu or a grain of millet.
translations.idiomatic: The Han, having restored order, sought to reform the old ways. Though they pursued simplified laws and reduced harsh penalties, they still practiced dismemberment and maintained prohibitions as minute as grains of millet.

sentences.zh: 字民之道，實有未弘，刑措之風，以茲莫致。

translations.literal: The way of nurturing the people was in truth not yet broadly applied; the wind of punishments set aside was on this account not attained.
translations.idiomatic: Their governance of the people had not yet reached its full breadth, and the ideal of punishments lying unused could not be realized.

sentences.zh: 爰及魏、晉，流弊相沿，寬猛乖方，綱維失序。

translations.literal: Down to Wei and Jin, flowing abuses continued in succession; lenience and severity lost their proper alignment, and the sustaining cords fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: By the Wei and Jin dynasties, abuses had accumulated through generations; leniency and severity were applied at cross purposes, and the bonds of governance fell into disorder.

sentences.zh: 下淩上替，政散民凋。

translations.literal: Inferiors encroached upon superiors and the superior order decayed; government scattered and the people withered.
translations.idiomatic: Inferiors overawed their superiors, government dissolved, and the people languished.

sentences.zh: 皆由法令湮訛，條章混謬。

translations.literal: All were due to statutes and ordinances having sunk into error and articles and regulations having become confused and mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: All of this stemmed from statutes that had fallen into confusion and regulations that had become muddled and contradictory.

sentences.zh: 自斯以後，宇縣瓜分，戎馬交馳，未遑典制。

translations.literal: From this time onward, the realm was carved up like a melon, war-horses charged against one another, and there was no leisure for canonical institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the realm was carved into rival domains, armies clashed without cease, and there was no leisure to establish proper institutions.

sentences.zh: 有隋之世，雖云厘革，然而損益不定，疏舛尚多，品式章程，罕能甄備。

translations.literal: In the age of Sui, though it was said that reforms were carried out, yet additions and reductions were not fixed, omissions and errors were still many, and categories, forms, and regulations were rarely able to be examined and made complete.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui, though reforms were proclaimed, revisions remained unsettled, errors and omissions abounded, and the categories and forms of the code were rarely brought to completion.

sentences.zh: 加以微文曲致，覽者惑其淺深，異例同科，用者殊其輕重，遂使奸吏巧詆，任情與奪，愚民妄觸，動陷羅網，屢聞厘革，卒以無成。

translations.literal: Added to this were subtle texts and tortuous applications, so that readers were confused as to their depth or shallowness; different precedents were placed in the same category, and those who applied them made their severity and lenience differ; thus crafty clerks ingeniously twisted the law, disposing of cases as their feelings dictated, while foolish commoners rashly transgressed and constantly fell into the net, and though reforms were repeatedly heard of, in the end nothing was accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, subtle clauses and tortuous applications left readers uncertain of their meaning; disparate cases were lumped under the same category, and magistrates applied them with inconsistent severity. Crafty officials twisted the law at will, while ignorant commoners stumbled unawares into the net of justice. Reforms were repeatedly announced, yet in the end nothing was achieved.

sentences.zh: 朕膺期受籙，甯濟區宇，永言至治，興寐為勞。

translations.literal: I have received the mandate in accord with the season and brought peace to the realm; ever speaking of perfect governance, I am wearied whether waking or sleeping.
translations.idiomatic: Having received the Mandate of Heaven in due season, I have brought peace to the realm; ever striving toward perfect governance, I labor whether waking or asleep.

sentences.zh: 補千年之墜典，拯百王之餘弊，思所以正本澄源，式清流末，永垂憲則，貽範後昆。

translations.literal: To repair fallen canons of a thousand years, to rescue the remaining abuses of a hundred kings, I ponder how to rectify the root and clarify the source, to set the pattern for clearing the turbid end, to hand down constitutional norms forever, and to bequeath a model to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: I seek to restore canons a thousand years fallen into neglect, to remedy the lingering abuses of a hundred reigns, to rectify the root and clarify the source, to set a standard for purging corruption at its farthest reach, and to establish constitutional norms that will endure as a model for generations to come.

sentences.zh: 爰命群才，修定科律。

translations.literal: I therefore command the assembled talents to revise and fix the statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: I have therefore charged men of talent to revise and complete the code.

sentences.zh: 但今古異務，文質不同，喪亂之後，事殊曩代，應機適變，救弊斯在。

translations.literal: Yet the tasks of past and present differ, and ornament and substance are not the same; after the age of ruin and disorder, affairs are unlike those of former generations; to respond to the moment and suit change, to remedy abuses—herein lies the point.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the tasks of past and present differ, and the forms of law must change with the times. After an age of ruin and disorder, affairs are unlike those of former dynasties; the need is to adapt to circumstances and remedy present abuses.

sentences.zh: 是以斟酌繁省，取合時宜，矯正差遺，務從體要。

translations.literal: Therefore we weigh what is complex and what is simplified, taking what accords with the fitness of the time, correcting errors and omissions, striving to follow the essential substance.
translations.idiomatic: We have therefore weighed what to retain and what to simplify, adapting the code to present needs, correcting errors and omissions, and adhering to essentials.

sentences.zh: 迄茲曆稔，撰次始畢，宜下四方，即令頒用。

translations.literal: Until now, over successive years, compilation has at last been completed; it is fitting to send it down to the four quarters and immediately order its promulgation and use.
translations.idiomatic: After years of labor the compilation is at last complete. Let it be sent throughout the realm and put into immediate effect.

sentences.zh: 庶使吏曹簡肅，無取懸石之多；

translations.literal: May it cause the offices of clerks to be simple and austere, not taking on the multitude of hanging stones;
translations.idiomatic: May the offices of clerks be simplified and disciplined, no longer burdened with volumes as weighty as hanging stones;

sentences.zh: 奏讞平允，靡競錐刀之末。

translations.literal: reports of judgments be even and fair, and none contend over the tip of an awl or knife.
translations.idiomatic: judgments reported to the throne be fair and even-handed, and none wrangle over the pettiest legal niceties.

sentences.zh: 勝殘去殺，此焉非遠。

translations.literal: To overcome the cruel and remove killing—this is not far from here.
translations.idiomatic: To overcome cruelty and abolish capital punishment—this goal is not far to seek.

sentences.zh: 於是頒行天下。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The code was then promulgated throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 及太宗即位，又命長孫無忌、房玄齡與學士法官，更加厘改。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, he again ordered Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, and the academicians and judges of the law to make further revisions and corrections.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong ascended the throne, he again charged Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, and the legal scholars and judges with further revision of the code.

sentences.zh: 戴胄、魏徵又言舊律令重，于時議絞刑之屬五十條。

translations.literal: Dai Zhou and Wei Zheng also said that the old statutes and ordinances were severe; at that time fifty articles belonging to the category of strangulation were discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Zhou and Wei Zheng also argued that the old code was too severe; at that time fifty articles carrying the death penalty by strangulation were under discussion.

sentences.zh: 免死罪，斷其右趾，應死者多蒙全活。

translations.literal: Exempting them from the death penalty, their right toes were severed; of those who should have died, many received preservation of life.
translations.idiomatic: They were spared execution and instead had their right foot amputated; many who would otherwise have died were allowed to live.

sentences.zh: 太宗尋又湣其受刑之苦，謂侍臣曰：「前代不行肉刑久矣，今忽斷人右趾，意甚不忍。

translations.literal: Before long Taizong again pitied their suffering under punishment and said to his attending ministers: "Former ages have long ceased to practice bodily punishments; now suddenly to sever men's right toes—my heart is deeply unwilling."
translations.idiomatic: Before long Taizong again took pity on their suffering and told his ministers, "Former dynasties long ago abandoned bodily mutilation as punishment. To suddenly amputate a man's right foot—I find this deeply distressing."

sentences.zh: 」諫議大夫王珪對曰：「古行肉刑，以為輕罪。

translations.literal: " Remonstrating Counselor Wang Gui replied: "In antiquity bodily punishments were practiced, taking them as light offenses."
translations.idiomatic: " Remonstrating Counselor Wang Gui replied, "In antiquity bodily punishments were applied to lesser offenses."

sentences.zh: 今陛下矜死刑之多，設斷趾之法，格本合死，今而獲生。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty pities the multitude of death sentences and has established the law of severing the toes; those who by the statute ought to die now obtain life.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, pitying the great number of death sentences, established amputation of the foot as an alternative. Those who by statute deserved death now received life.

sentences.zh: 刑者幸得全命，豈憚去其一足？

translations.literal: Those punished are fortunate to preserve their lives in full—how would they shrink from losing one foot?
translations.idiomatic: The condemned, fortunate to preserve their lives, would hardly shrink from losing a foot.

sentences.zh: 且人之見者，甚足懲誡。

translations.literal: Moreover, for those who see them, it is quite sufficient for warning and admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the sight of them would serve as ample warning to others.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「本以為寬，故行之。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Originally I took it to be lenient, and therefore put it into practice."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "I adopted it in the belief that it was lenient, and therefore put it into practice."

sentences.zh: 然每聞惻愴，不能忘懷。

translations.literal: Yet whenever I hear of it I am filled with compassion and cannot put it from my mind.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever I hear of it I am filled with compassion and cannot put it from my mind.

sentences.zh: 」又謂蕭瑀、陳叔達等曰：「朕以死者不可再生，思有矜湣，故簡死罪五十條，從斷右趾。

translations.literal: " He also said to Xiao Yu, Chen Shuda, and others: "I take the view that the dead cannot live again; thinking to show compassion and pity, I therefore selected fifty death-penalty articles and substituted severing the right toe."
translations.idiomatic: " He also said to Xiao Yu, Chen Shuda, and others, "The dead cannot be restored to life. Seeking to show compassion, I selected fifty capital offenses and substituted amputation of the right foot."

sentences.zh: 朕復念其受痛，極所不忍。

translations.literal: I again reflect on their suffering pain—this is what I most cannot bear.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when I reflect on the pain they endure, I find it almost unbearable.

sentences.zh: 」叔達等咸曰：「古之肉刑，乃在死刑之外。

translations.literal: " Shuda and the others all said: "The bodily punishments of antiquity were outside the death penalty."
translations.idiomatic: " Shuda and the others all replied, "In antiquity bodily punishments were applied in addition to, not in place of, the death penalty."

sentences.zh: 陛下于死刑之內，改從斷趾，便是以生易死，足為寬法。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, within the death penalty, changed it to severing the toes—this is to exchange life for death, and is fully sufficient as a lenient law.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, by substituting amputation for execution within the category of capital crimes, exchanged life for death—this is surely a lenient measure.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「朕意以為如此，故欲行之。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "My intention was that it was thus, and therefore I wished to put it into practice."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "That was my intention, and therefore I wished to put it into practice."

sentences.zh: 又有上書言此非便，公可更思之。

translations.literal: Moreover, there was a memorial saying that this was not convenient; you, sirs, may reconsider it further."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, a memorial has been submitted arguing that this measure is impracticable. Gentlemen, reconsider the matter."

sentences.zh: 」其後蜀王法曹參軍裴弘獻又駁律令不便於時者四十餘事，太宗令參掌刪改之。

translations.literal: " Thereafter Pei Hongxian, Legal Affairs Staff Officer under the Prince of Shu, again refuted more than forty matters in the statutes and ordinances that were inconvenient for the time, and Taizong ordered him to participate in supervising their deletion and revision.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereafter Pei Hongxian, a legal affairs officer under the Prince of Shu, submitted more than forty objections to provisions of the code ill suited to the times, and Taizong ordered him to participate in their revision.

sentences.zh: 弘獻於是與玄齡等建議，以為古者五刑，刖居其一。

translations.literal: Hongxian thereupon joined with Xuanling and others in proposing that in antiquity there were five punishments, and amputation of the foot occupied one of them.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxian thereupon joined Fang Xuanling and others in proposing that in antiquity there were five punishments, of which amputation of the foot was one.

sentences.zh: 及肉刑廢，制為死、流、杖、笞凡五等，以備五刑。

translations.literal: When bodily punishments were abolished, they were regulated as death, exile, beating with the staff, and beating with the rod—altogether five grades—to supply the five punishments.
translations.idiomatic: When bodily punishments were abolished, death, exile, beating with the staff, and beating with the rod were instituted as five grades to replace the five punishments.

sentences.zh: 今復設刖足，昌為六刑。

translations.literal: Now to establish amputation of the foot again is to make how many—six punishments?
translations.idiomatic: To reintroduce amputation of the foot is to create a sixth category of punishment.

sentences.zh: 減死在於寬弘，加刑又加煩峻。

translations.literal: Reducing death lies in lenience and breadth; adding punishments again adds what is burdensome and severe.
translations.idiomatic: Sparing offenders from death is an act of leniency, but adding a new punishment only increases severity and complexity.

sentences.zh: 乃與八座定議奏聞，於是又除斷趾法，改為加役流三千里，居作二年。

translations.literal: They then joined with the eight chief ministers in fixing the deliberation and reporting it; thereupon the law of severing the toes was again abolished and changed to penal servitude added to exile for three thousand li, with labor for two years.
translations.idiomatic: They joined the eight chief ministers in deliberation and reported their decision. The law of amputation was abolished and replaced by exile to a distance of three thousand li with two years of penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 又舊條疏，兄弟分後，廕不相及，連坐俱死，祖孫配沒。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the old articles and commentaries, when brothers had divided their households, hereditary privilege did not extend to one another, yet collective liability made all die together, and grandparents and grandchildren were sentenced to confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, under the old code, when brothers had established separate households they were not liable for one another's hereditary privileges, yet collective punishment still required all to die together, and grandparents and grandchildren were sentenced to confiscation of property.

sentences.zh: 會有同州人房強，弟任統軍於岷州，以謀反伏誅，強當從坐。

translations.literal: It happened that one Fang Qiang of Tongzhou had a younger brother serving as army commander at Minzhou who was executed for plotting rebellion; Qiang was to suffer collective liability.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Fang Qiang of Tongzhou had a younger brother serving as army commander at Minzhou who was executed for treason; Qiang was liable to collective punishment.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗錄囚徒，憫其將死，為之動容。

translations.literal: Taizong once reviewed prisoners and pitied those about to die, his countenance moved on their account.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once reviewed the prisoners and, pitying those about to die, was visibly moved.

sentences.zh: 顧謂侍臣曰：「刑典仍用，蓋風化未洽之咎。

translations.literal: Turning, he said to his attending ministers: "That the penal code is still in use is surely the fault of customs and transformation not having permeated fully."
translations.idiomatic: Turning to his ministers he said, "That the penal code is still in use reflects the failure of moral transformation to permeate society fully."

sentences.zh: 愚人何罪，而肆重刑乎？

translations.literal: What crime have foolish men committed, that heavy punishments are applied so freely?
translations.idiomatic: What crime have these simple men committed, that such heavy punishments are inflicted upon them?

sentences.zh: 更彰朕之不德也。

translations.literal: This further displays my lack of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: This only highlights my own want of virtue.

sentences.zh: 用刑之道，當審事理之輕重，然後加之以刑罰。

translations.literal: The way of applying punishments is to examine carefully the lightness or heaviness of the matter and principle, and only then add punishments upon them.
translations.idiomatic: The proper application of punishment requires careful weighing of the gravity of each case before penalties are imposed.

sentences.zh: 何有不察其本而一概加誅，非所以恤刑重人命也。

translations.literal: How can there be failure to examine their root and indiscriminate application of execution? This is not the means to show compassion in punishments and value human lives.
translations.idiomatic: How can we fail to examine the root of each case and apply execution indiscriminately? This is not the way to show compassion in punishment and value human life.

sentences.zh: 然則反逆有二：一為興師動眾，一為惡言犯法。

translations.literal: Thus rebellion has two kinds: one is raising troops and moving the masses; one is evil words violating the law.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion, then, takes two forms: one is raising armies and mobilizing forces; the other is seditious speech in violation of the law.

sentences.zh: 輕重有差，而連坐皆死，豈朕情之所安哉？

translations.literal: In severity and lenience there are differences, yet collective liability makes all die—how can this be what my feelings can rest content with?
translations.idiomatic: These differ greatly in severity, yet collective punishment condemns all to death alike—how can my conscience accept this?

sentences.zh: 」更令百僚詳議。

translations.literal: " He further ordered the hundred officials to deliberate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered the officials to deliberate the matter in detail.

sentences.zh: 於是玄齡等復定議曰：「案禮，孫為王父屍。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xuanling and others again fixed their deliberation, saying: "According to the Rites, the grandson serves as the corpse-substitute for the grandfather on the father's side."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Fang Xuanling and others submitted their deliberation: "According to the Rites, a grandson serves as the ritual substitute for his paternal grandfather."

sentences.zh: 案令，祖有廕孫之義。

translations.literal: According to the ordinances, the grandfather has the principle of hereditary privilege extending to the grandson.
translations.idiomatic: According to the ordinances, a grandfather may confer hereditary privilege upon his grandson.

sentences.zh: 然則祖孫親重而兄弟屬輕，應重反流，合輕翻死，據禮論情，深為未愜。

translations.literal: Thus the bond between grandfather and grandson is weighty while the tie among brothers is light; what should be heavy is instead sent into exile, and what should be light is turned into death—judging by ritual and weighing feeling, this is deeply unsatisfying.
translations.idiomatic: The bond between grandfather and grandson is weightier than that among brothers, yet the heavier tie receives exile while the lighter tie receives death. Judged by ritual propriety and human feeling, this is deeply unsatisfactory.

sentences.zh: 今定律，祖孫與兄弟緣坐，俱配沒。

translations.literal: Now in fixing the law, grandparents and grandchildren together with brothers suffer collective liability and are all sentenced to confiscation and exile.
translations.idiomatic: Under the present code, grandparents, grandchildren, and brothers alike suffer collective liability and are sentenced to confiscation and exile.

sentences.zh: 其以惡言犯法不能為害者，情狀稍輕，兄弟免死，配流為允。

translations.literal: For those who by evil words violate the law but cannot do harm, the circumstances are somewhat lighter; brothers should be exempted from death and sentenced to confiscation and exile—this is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Where the offense consists of seditious speech that could do no actual harm, the circumstances are lighter; brothers should be spared death and sentenced to exile—this we deem acceptable.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " [The emperor] followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 自是比古死刑，殆除其半。

translations.literal: From this time, compared with the death penalties of antiquity, nearly half were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: From this point onward, nearly half the capital offenses of earlier ages were eliminated.

sentences.zh: 玄齡等遂與法司定律五百條，分為十二卷：一曰名例，二曰衛禁，三曰職制，四曰戶婚，五曰廄庫，六曰擅興，七曰賊盜，八曰鬥訟，九曰詐偽，十曰雜律，十一曰捕亡，十二曰斷獄。

translations.literal: Xuanling and others thereupon joined with the legal offices in fixing five hundred articles of law, divided into twelve scrolls: first, General Principles; second, Palace and Frontier Prohibitions; third, Official Regulations; fourth, Households and Marriage; fifth, Stables and Storehouses; sixth, Unauthorized Mobilization; seventh, Banditry and Theft; eighth, Assault and Litigation; ninth, Fraud and Forgery; tenth, Miscellaneous Statutes; eleventh, Apprehension of Fugitives; twelfth, Trial and Judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling and his colleagues, working with the judicial offices, compiled five hundred statutes in twelve sections: General Principles; Palace and Frontier Prohibitions; Official Regulations; Households and Marriage; Stables and Storehouses; Unauthorized Mobilization; Banditry and Theft; Assault and Litigation; Fraud and Forgery; Miscellaneous Statutes; Apprehension of Fugitives; and Trial and Judgment.

sentences.zh: 有笞、杖、徒、流、死，為五刑。

translations.literal: There were beating with the rod, beating with the staff, penal servitude, exile, and death—these constituted the five punishments.
translations.idiomatic: The five punishments were beating with the rod, beating with the staff, penal servitude, exile, and death.

sentences.zh: 笞刑五條，自笞十至五十；

translations.literal: Rod punishments, five articles, from ten strokes to fifty;
translations.idiomatic: Rod punishments comprised five grades, from ten to fifty strokes;

sentences.zh: 杖刑五條，自杖六十至杖一百；

translations.literal: Staff punishments, five articles, from sixty strokes to one hundred strokes;
translations.idiomatic: Staff punishments comprised five grades, from sixty to one hundred strokes;

sentences.zh: 徒刑五條，自徒一年，遞加半年，至三年；

translations.literal: Penal servitude, five articles, from one year, increasing by half a year at each step, up to three years;
translations.idiomatic: Penal servitude comprised five grades, from one year, increasing by half a year at each step, up to three years;

sentences.zh: 流刑三條，自流二千里，遞加五百里，至三千里；

translations.literal: Exile, three articles, from exile for two thousand li, increasing by five hundred li at each step, up to three thousand li;
translations.idiomatic: Exile comprised three grades, from two thousand li, increasing by five hundred li at each step, up to three thousand li;

sentences.zh: 死刑二條：絞、斬。

translations.literal: death penalty, two articles: strangulation and decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: capital punishment two forms: strangulation and decapitation.

sentences.zh: 大凡二十等。

translations.literal: In all there were twenty grades.
translations.idiomatic: In all there were twenty grades of punishment.

sentences.zh: 又有議請減贖當免之法八：一曰議親，二曰議故，三曰議賢，四曰議能，五曰議功，六曰議貴，七曰議賓，八曰議勤。

translations.literal: There were also eight methods of deliberation, petition, reduction, commutation, and exemption: first, deliberation for kin; second, deliberation for old associates; third, deliberation for worthies; fourth, deliberation for ability; fifth, deliberation for merit; sixth, deliberation for nobility; seventh, deliberation for guests; eighth, deliberation for diligence.
translations.idiomatic: There were also eight categories of statutory privilege—deliberation, petition, reduction, commutation, and exemption: deliberation for kin, for old associates, for worthies, for ability, for merit, for nobility, for guests, and for diligence.

sentences.zh: 八議者，犯死罪者皆條所坐及應議之狀奏請，議定奏裁。

translations.literal: For the eight deliberations, all who committed death-penalty crimes were to set forth the offense charged and the circumstances warranting deliberation in a memorial petition; after deliberation was fixed, it was memorialized for imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: Under the eight deliberations, all capital offenders were required to submit a memorial setting forth the offense and the grounds for deliberation; after deliberation the case was submitted for imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 流罪已下，減一等。

translations.literal: For exile and below, one grade was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: For exile and lesser offenses, the penalty was reduced by one grade.

sentences.zh: 若官爵五品已上，及皇太子妃大功已上親，應議者周以上親，犯死罪者上請。

translations.literal: If of official rank and nobility of the fifth grade and above, and relatives within great mourning of the crown prince's consort, and relatives within the circle of those eligible for deliberation—relatives within the circle and above—who committed death-penalty crimes, they were to submit a petition upward.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the fifth rank and above, relatives within the great-mourning circle of the crown prince's consort, and relatives within the circle of those eligible for deliberation who committed capital offenses were required to submit a petition for imperial review.

sentences.zh: 流罪已下，亦減一等。

translations.literal: For exile and below, one grade was also reduced.
translations.idiomatic: For exile and lesser offenses, the penalty was likewise reduced by one grade.

sentences.zh: 若七品已上官，及官爵得請者之祖父母、父母、兄弟、姊妹、妻、子孫，犯流罪已下，各減一等。

translations.literal: If officials of the seventh grade and above, and the grandparents, parents, brothers, sisters, wives, and children and grandchildren of those whose official rank and nobility entitled them to petition—who committed exile and below—each had one grade reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the seventh rank and above, and the grandparents, parents, siblings, wives, and descendants of those entitled to petition who committed exile or lesser offenses, each received a reduction of one grade.

sentences.zh: 若應議請減及九品已上官，若官品得減者之祖父母、父母、妻、子孫，犯流罪已下，聽贖。

translations.literal: If eligible for deliberation, petition, and reduction, and officials of the ninth grade and above, and the grandparents, parents, wives, and children and grandchildren of those whose official rank entitled them to reduction—who committed exile and below—commutation was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Those eligible for deliberation, petition, or reduction, officials of the ninth rank and above, and the grandparents, parents, wives, and descendants of those entitled to reduction who committed exile or lesser offenses were permitted to commute their penalties.

sentences.zh: 其贖法：笞十，贖銅一斤，遞加一斤，至杖一百，則贖銅十斤。

translations.literal: The method of commutation: for ten strokes of the rod, one jin of copper; increasing by one jin at each step, up to one hundred strokes of the staff, then ten jin of copper.
translations.idiomatic: The commutation rates were as follows: ten strokes of the rod, one jin of copper; increasing by one jin at each step, up to one hundred strokes of the staff, for which ten jin of copper was required.

sentences.zh: 自此已上，遞加十斤，至徒三年，則贖銅六十斤。

translations.literal: From this upward, increasing by ten jin at each step, up to three years of penal servitude, then sixty jin of copper.
translations.idiomatic: Above this level the rate increased by ten jin at each step, up to three years of penal servitude, for which sixty jin of copper was required.

sentences.zh: 流二千里者，贖銅八十斤；

translations.literal: For exile of two thousand li, eighty jin of copper;
translations.idiomatic: For exile of two thousand li, eighty jin of copper;

sentences.zh: 流二千五百里者，贖銅九十斤；

translations.literal: for exile of two thousand five hundred li, ninety jin of copper;
translations.idiomatic: for exile of two thousand five hundred li, ninety jin of copper;

sentences.zh: 流三千里者，贖銅一百斤。

translations.literal: for exile of three thousand li, one hundred jin of copper.
translations.idiomatic: for exile of three thousand li, one hundred jin of copper.

sentences.zh: 絞斬者，贖銅一百二十斤。

translations.literal: For strangulation and decapitation, one hundred twenty jin of copper.
translations.idiomatic: For strangulation and decapitation, one hundred twenty jin of copper.

sentences.zh: 又許以官當罪。

translations.literal: It was also permitted to use office to offset punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Official rank could also be used to offset punishment.

sentences.zh: 以官當徒者，五品已上犯私罪者，一官當徒二年；

translations.literal: For using office to offset penal servitude: for those of the fifth grade and above who committed private offenses, one office offset two years of penal servitude;
translations.idiomatic: When office was used to offset penal servitude, officials of the fifth rank and above who committed private offenses could offset two years of penal servitude with one office;

sentences.zh: 九品已上，一官當徒一年。

translations.literal: for those of the ninth grade and above, one office offset one year of penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: officials of the ninth rank and above could offset one year with one office.

sentences.zh: 若犯公罪者，各加一年。

translations.literal: If they committed public offenses, one year was added in each case.
translations.idiomatic: For public offenses, one year was added in each case.

sentences.zh: 以官當流者，三流同比徒四年，仍各解見任。

translations.literal: For using office to offset exile: the three grades of exile were together equivalent to four years of penal servitude, and in each case the incumbent office was removed.
translations.idiomatic: When office was used to offset exile, all three grades of exile were equivalent to four years of penal servitude, and the incumbent was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 除名者，比徒三年。

translations.literal: Removal from the registers was equivalent to three years of penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Removal from official registers was equivalent to three years of penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 免官者，比徒二年。

translations.literal: Dismissal from office was equivalent to two years of penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissal from office was equivalent to two years of penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 免所居官者，比徒一年。

translations.literal: Removal from the office held was equivalent to one year of penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Removal from the office then held was equivalent to one year of penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 又有十惡之條：一曰謀反，二曰謀大逆，三曰謀叛，四曰謀惡逆，五曰不道，六曰大不敬，七曰不孝，八曰不睦，九曰不義，十曰內亂。

translations.literal: There were also the ten abominations: first, plotting rebellion; second, plotting great sedition; third, plotting defection; fourth, plotting wicked sedition; fifth, depravity; sixth, great irreverence; seventh, unfilial conduct; eighth, discord within the clan; ninth, unrighteous conduct; tenth, internal disorder.
translations.idiomatic: There were also the ten abominations: plotting rebellion, plotting great sedition, plotting defection, plotting wicked sedition, depravity, great irreverence, unfilial conduct, discord within the clan, unrighteous conduct, and internal disorder.

sentences.zh: 其犯十惡者，不得依議請之例。

translations.literal: Those who committed the ten abominations could not rely on the precedents of deliberation and petition.
translations.idiomatic: Those who committed any of the ten abominations were ineligible for deliberation, petition, or commutation.

sentences.zh: 年七十以上、十五以下及廢疾，犯流罪以下，亦聽贖。

translations.literal: Those seventy years and above, fifteen and below, and the crippled and disabled who committed exile and below were also permitted to commute.
translations.idiomatic: Persons seventy years of age or older, fifteen or younger, or suffering from crippling disability who committed exile or lesser offenses were also permitted to commute their penalties.

sentences.zh: 八十已上、十歲以下及篤疾，犯反逆殺人應死者，上請，盜及傷人，亦收贖，餘皆勿論。

translations.literal: Those eighty and above, ten years and below, and those with grave illness who committed rebellion, sedition, or murder warranting death were to submit a petition upward; for theft and wounding people, commutation was also accepted; all else was not prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Persons eighty or older, ten or younger, or suffering grave illness who committed rebellion, sedition, or capital murder were required to petition for imperial review; theft and assault were subject to commutation; all other offenses were not prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 九十以上、七歲以下，雖有死罪，不加刑。

translations.literal: Those ninety and above and seven years and below, though having death-penalty crimes, were not subjected to punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Persons ninety or older and seven or younger, though guilty of capital crimes, were not subjected to punishment.

sentences.zh: 比隋代舊律，減大辟者九十二條，減流入徒者七十一條。

translations.literal: Compared with the old code of the Sui, capital offenses were reduced by ninety-two articles, and exile reduced to penal servitude by seventy-one articles.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with the Sui code, capital offenses were reduced by ninety-two articles and exile converted to penal servitude by seventy-one articles.

sentences.zh: 其當徒之法，唯奪一官，除名之人，仍同士伍。

translations.literal: The method of offsetting penal servitude took only one office; those removed from the registers were still treated the same as common soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When office was used to offset penal servitude, only one office was forfeited; those removed from the registers were still conscripted as common soldiers.

sentences.zh: 凡削煩去蠹，變重為輕者，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: In all, the cutting away of complexity and removal of abuses, changing the heavy into the light—these cannot be fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The simplifications and reductions in severity were too numerous to record in full.

sentences.zh: 又定令一千五百九十條，為三十卷。

translations.literal: They also fixed ordinances in one thousand five hundred ninety articles, in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: They also compiled one thousand five hundred ninety administrative ordinances in thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十一年正月，頒下之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year of Zhenguan they were promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eleventh year of Zhenguan they were promulgated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 又刪武德、貞觀已來敕格三千餘件，定留七百條，以為格十八卷，留本司施行。

translations.literal: They also deleted more than three thousand edicts and regulations from Wude and Zhenguan onward, fixing seven hundred articles to remain, making them into eighteen scrolls of regulations, retained by the originating offices for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: More than three thousand edicts and regulations issued since the Wude and Zhenguan eras were reviewed, and seven hundred articles were retained as eighteen scrolls of supplementary regulations for implementation by the originating offices.

sentences.zh: 斟酌今古，除煩去弊，甚為寬簡，便於人者。

translations.literal: Weighing past and present, removing complexity and eliminating abuses, they were very lenient and simple, convenient for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Weighing past and present practice, complexity and abuse were eliminated; the result was notably lenient, simple, and convenient for the people.

sentences.zh: 以尚書省諸曹為之目，初為七卷。

translations.literal: Taking the various bureaus of the Department of State Affairs as its categories, it was at first seven scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Organized under the bureaus of the Department of State Affairs, it initially comprised seven scrolls.

sentences.zh: 其曹之常條，但留本司者，別為《留司格》一卷。

translations.literal: The standing articles of each bureau that were retained only by the originating office were separately made into one scroll of Retained Bureau Regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Standing regulations retained only by the originating bureau were separately compiled as one scroll of Retained Bureau Regulations.

sentences.zh: 蓋編錄當時制敕，永為法則，以為故事。

translations.literal: These in general compiled the edicts and orders of the time, to be constitutional norms forever, taken as precedents.
translations.idiomatic: These compiled contemporary edicts and orders as permanent legal norms and precedents.

sentences.zh: 《貞觀格》十八卷，房玄齡等刪定。

translations.literal: The Zhenguan Regulations in eighteen scrolls were revised and fixed by Fang Xuanling and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenguan Regulations in eighteen scrolls were compiled by Fang Xuanling and his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 《永徽留司格》十八卷，《散頒格》七卷，長孫無忌等刪定，永徽中，又令源直心等刪定，惟改易官號曹局之名，不易篇目。

translations.literal: The Yonghui Retained Bureau Regulations in eighteen scrolls and the Broadly Promulgated Regulations in seven scrolls were revised by Zhangsun Wuji and others; in the Yonghui period, Yuan Zhixin and others were again ordered to revise them, changing only the names of offices and bureaus, not the section titles.
translations.idiomatic: The Yonghui Retained Bureau Regulations in eighteen scrolls and the Broadly Promulgated Regulations in seven scrolls were compiled by Zhangsun Wuji and others. During the Yonghui era Yuan Zhixin and others revised them, changing only office and bureau titles while leaving the section headings unchanged.

sentences.zh: 《永徽留司格後本》，劉仁軌等刪定。

translations.literal: The Later Edition of the Yonghui Retained Bureau Regulations was revised by Liu Rengui and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Edition of the Yonghui Retained Bureau Regulations was compiled by Liu Rengui and others.

sentences.zh: 《垂拱留司格》六卷，《散頒格》三卷，裴居道刪定。

translations.literal: The Chuigong Retained Bureau Regulations in six scrolls and the Broadly Promulgated Regulations in three scrolls were revised by Pei Judao.
translations.idiomatic: The Chuigong Retained Bureau Regulations in six scrolls and the Broadly Promulgated Regulations in three scrolls were compiled by Pei Judao.

sentences.zh: 《太極格》十卷，岑羲等刪定。

translations.literal: The Taiji Regulations in ten scrolls were revised by Cen Xi and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Taiji Regulations in ten scrolls were compiled by Cen Xi and others.

sentences.zh: 《開元前格》十卷，姚崇等刪定。

translations.literal: The Pre-Kaiyuan Regulations in ten scrolls were revised by Yao Chong and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Pre-Kaiyuan Regulations in ten scrolls were compiled by Yao Chong and others.

sentences.zh: 《開元後格》十卷，宋璟等刪定。

translations.literal: The Post-Kaiyuan Regulations in ten scrolls were revised by Song Jing and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Post-Kaiyuan Regulations in ten scrolls were compiled by Song Jing and others.

sentences.zh: 皆以尚書省二十四司為篇目。

translations.literal: All took the twenty-four bureaus of the Department of State Affairs as their section titles.
translations.idiomatic: All were organized under the twenty-four bureaus of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 凡式三十有三篇，亦以尚書省列曹及秘書、太常、司農、光祿、太僕、太府、少府及監門、宿衛、計帳名其篇目，為二十卷。

translations.literal: In all there were thirty-three sections of Forms, also taking the various bureaus of the Department of State Affairs and the Secretariat, Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Ministry of Agriculture, Court of Imperial Entertainments, Court of the Imperial Stud, Court of the Imperial Treasury, Court of the Imperial Manufactories, and the Directorate of Gate Guards, Palace Guards, and Accounts as their section titles, in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: There were thirty-three sections of Forms, organized under the bureaus of the Department of State Affairs and the Secretariat, Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Ministry of Agriculture, Court of Imperial Entertainments, Court of the Imperial Stud, Court of the Imperial Treasury, Court of the Imperial Manufactories, Directorate of Gate Guards, Palace Guards, and Accounts, in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 《永徽式》十四卷，《垂拱》、《神龍》、《開元式》並二十卷，其刪定格令同。

translations.literal: The Yonghui Forms in fourteen scrolls; the Chuigong, Shenlong, and Kaiyuan Forms each in twenty scrolls—their revision and fixing of regulations and ordinances was the same.
translations.idiomatic: The Yonghui Forms comprised fourteen scrolls; the Chuigong, Shenlong, and Kaiyuan Forms each comprised twenty scrolls. The process of revision was the same as for the statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 太宗又制在京見禁囚，刑部每月一奏，從立春至秋分，不得奏決死刑。

translations.literal: Taizong also regulated that for prisoners currently detained in the capital, the Ministry of Justice was to report monthly; from the Beginning of Spring to the Autumn Equinox, death sentences were not to be reported for decision.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong also decreed that prisoners detained in the capital were to be reported monthly by the Ministry of Justice, and that from the Beginning of Spring to the Autumn Equinox no death sentences were to be submitted for approval.

sentences.zh: 其大祭祀及致齋、朔望、上下弦、二十四氣、雨未晴、夜未明、斷屠日月及假日，並不得奏決死刑。

translations.literal: On great sacrifices and days of ritual abstinence, the new and full moon, the first and third quarter moon, the twenty-four solar terms, days when rain had not cleared, nights not yet bright, days of prohibition on slaughter, and holidays—on all these, death sentences were not to be reported for decision.
translations.idiomatic: Death sentences were also prohibited on days of great sacrifice, ritual abstinence, new and full moon, quarter moons, the twenty-four solar terms, days of unbroken rain, nights before dawn, days when slaughter was forbidden, and holidays.

sentences.zh: 其有赦之日，武庫令設金雞及鼓于宮城門外之右，勒集囚徒于闕前，撾鼓千聲訖，宣詔而釋之。

translations.literal: On days when there was an amnesty, the Director of the Armory set up a golden rooster and a drum to the right outside the palace-city gate, assembled the prisoners before the palace gate, and when a thousand beats of the drum were finished, proclaimed the edict and released them.
translations.idiomatic: On days of amnesty the Director of the Armory set up a golden rooster and drum to the right of the palace gate, assembled the prisoners before the palace, and after a thousand drumbeats proclaimed the edict of release.

sentences.zh: 其赦書頒諸州，用絹寫行下。

translations.literal: The amnesty document was promulgated to all prefectures, written on silk and sent down.
translations.idiomatic: The amnesty document was promulgated to all prefectures, transcribed on silk and distributed.

sentences.zh: 又系囚之具，有枷、杻鉗、鎖，皆有長短廣狹之制，量罪輕重，節級用之。

translations.literal: Moreover, the implements for restraining prisoners included cangues, manacles, fetters, and locks, all having regulations for length, shortness, breadth, and narrowness; according to the lightness or heaviness of the offense, they were applied by graded steps.
translations.idiomatic: Restraints for prisoners included cangues, manacles, fetters, and locks, each regulated as to dimensions and applied in graded steps according to the severity of the offense.

sentences.zh: 其杖皆削去節目，長三尺五寸。

translations.literal: The staffs all had their nodes shaved away and were three chi five cun in length.
translations.idiomatic: All beating staffs had their nodes removed and measured three chi five cun in length.

sentences.zh: 訊囚杖，大頭徑三分二厘，小頭二分二厘。

translations.literal: Interrogation staffs: the large end three fen two li in diameter, the small end two fen two li.
translations.idiomatic: Interrogation staffs measured three fen two li in diameter at the large end and two fen two li at the small end.

sentences.zh: 常行杖，大頭二分七厘，小頭一分七厘。

translations.literal: Ordinary execution staffs: large end two fen seven li, small end one fen seven li.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary execution staffs measured two fen seven li at the large end and one fen seven li at the small end.

sentences.zh: 笞杖，大頭二分，小頭一分半。

translations.literal: Rod staffs: large end two fen, small end one fen and a half.
translations.idiomatic: Rod staffs measured two fen at the large end and one and a half fen at the small end.

sentences.zh: 其決笞者，腿分受。

translations.literal: For those receiving rod punishment, the strokes were divided between the legs.
translations.idiomatic: Rod punishments were administered on the legs in rotation.

sentences.zh: 決杖者，背、腿、臀分受。

translations.literal: For those receiving staff punishment, the back, legs, and buttocks received strokes in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Staff punishments were administered on the back, legs, and buttocks in rotation.

sentences.zh: 及須數等拷訊者，亦同。

translations.literal: For those requiring repeated interrogation by beating, it was the same.
translations.idiomatic: The same rule applied to repeated interrogation by beating.

sentences.zh: 其拷囚不過三度，總數不得過二百。

translations.literal: Interrogation of prisoners was not to exceed three rounds; the total number of strokes was not to exceed two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Interrogation by beating was limited to three sessions and two hundred strokes in total.

sentences.zh: 杖罪已下，不得過所犯之數。

translations.literal: For staff offenses and below, [the strokes] were not to exceed the number prescribed for the offense committed.
translations.idiomatic: For staff punishments and below, the strokes administered could not exceed the statutory number for the offense.

sentences.zh: 諸斷罪而無正條，其應出罪者，則舉重以明輕；

translations.literal: For all cases of judgment where there was no proper article, if the offense should result in acquittal, then cite the heavy to clarify the light;
translations.idiomatic: When no statute directly applied to a case, if acquittal was warranted the judge cited a heavier analogous offense to establish the lighter principle;

sentences.zh: 其應入罪者，則舉輕以明重。

translations.literal: if the offense should result in conviction, then cite the light to clarify the heavy.
translations.idiomatic: if conviction was warranted, he cited a lighter analogous offense to establish the heavier principle.

sentences.zh: 稱加者，就重次；

translations.literal: Where it says "increase," proceed to the heavier grade;
translations.idiomatic: Where the code specified an increase in penalty, the next heavier grade was applied;

sentences.zh: 稱減者，就輕次。

translations.literal: where it says "reduce," proceed to the lighter grade.
translations.idiomatic: where it specified a reduction, the next lighter grade was applied.

sentences.zh: 惟二死三流，同為一減，不得加至於死。

translations.literal: Only the two death penalties and three exiles counted as one reduction together; [penalties] could not be increased to death.
translations.idiomatic: Only the two forms of capital punishment and the three grades of exile counted as a single reduction; no penalty could be increased to death.

sentences.zh: 斷獄而失於出入者，以其罪罪之。

translations.literal: Those who in trying cases erred in acquittal or conviction were punished according to their offense.
translations.idiomatic: Judges who erred in acquitting or convicting were themselves punished according to the offense involved.

sentences.zh: 失入者，各減三等；

translations.literal: For erroneous conviction, three grades were reduced in each case;
translations.idiomatic: For erroneous conviction, the judge's penalty was reduced by three grades;

sentences.zh: 失出者，各減五等。

translations.literal: for erroneous acquittal, five grades were reduced in each case.
translations.idiomatic: for erroneous acquittal, by five grades.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗以古者斷獄，必訊於三槐九棘之官，乃詔大辟罪，中書、門下五品已上及尚書等議之。

translations.literal: At first, Taizong, because in antiquity in trying cases one necessarily inquired of the officials of the three pagoda trees and nine thorn bushes, ordered that for great capital offenses, the Secretariat, Chancellery officials of the fifth grade and above, and the Department of State Affairs and others should deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Taizong, recalling that in antiquity capital cases were deliberated by the highest judicial officers, ordered that capital offenses be reviewed by officials of the Secretariat and Chancellery of the fifth rank and above and by the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 其後河內人李好德，風疾瞀亂，有妖妄之言，詔按其事。

translations.literal: Thereafter Li Haode of Henei, suffering from wind illness and mental confusion, uttered deluded and extravagant words; an edict was issued to investigate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Li Haode of Henei, afflicted with mental illness, uttered deluded and seditious words, and the emperor ordered an investigation.

sentences.zh: 大理丞張蘊古奏，好德癲病有征，法不當坐。

translations.literal: Assistant Grand Judge Zhang Yungu memorialized that Haode's epileptic illness had clear signs and that by law he should not be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Grand Judge Zhang Yungu memorialized that Haode showed clear signs of epilepsy and was not liable under the law.

sentences.zh: 治書侍御史權萬紀，劾蘊古貫相州，好德之兄厚德，為其刺史，情在阿縱，奏事不實。

translations.literal: Drafting Attending Censor Quan Wanji impeached Yungu, saying he had served as prefect of Xiangzhou, where Haode's elder brother Houde was prefect; his feelings were partial and indulgent, and his memorial was not truthful.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting Attending Censor Quan Wanji impeached Yungu, alleging that while serving as prefect of Xiangzhou—where Haode's elder brother Houde was also prefect—Yungu had shown partiality and submitted a false memorial.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「吾常禁囚於獄內，蘊古與之弈棋，今復阿縱好德，是亂吾法也。

translations.literal: Taizong said: "I once detained a prisoner in the prison, and Yungu played chess with him; now again he indulges Haode—this is to throw my laws into disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "I once detained a prisoner, and Yungu played chess with him. Now he indulges Haode again—this subverts my laws."

sentences.zh: 」遂斬於東市。

translations.literal: " He was thereupon executed at the Eastern Market.
translations.idiomatic: " Yungu was thereupon executed at the Eastern Market.

sentences.zh: 既而悔之。

translations.literal: Before long [the emperor] regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon regretted his decision.

sentences.zh: 又交州都督盧祖尚，以忤旨斬於朝堂，帝亦追悔。

translations.literal: Moreover, Regional Commander Lu Zushang of Jiaozhou was executed in the court hall for defying the imperial will, and the emperor also repented afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Lu Zushang of Jiaozhou was also executed in the court hall for defying an imperial order, and the emperor again repented.

sentences.zh: 下制，凡決死刑，雖令即殺，仍三覆奏。

translations.literal: He issued a regulation that for all death sentences decided, even if ordered for immediate execution, there must still be three re-submissions.
translations.idiomatic: He issued a regulation requiring three re-submissions for all death sentences, even when immediate execution was ordered.

sentences.zh: 尋謂侍臣曰：「人命至重，一死不可再生。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he said to his attending ministers: "Human life is of the utmost weight; once dead it cannot live again."
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter he told his ministers, "Human life is of the utmost weight; once taken it cannot be restored."

sentences.zh: 昔世充殺鄭頲，既而悔之，追止不及。

translations.literal: In the past Shichong killed Zheng Ting and afterward repented, but pursuit to halt it did not arrive in time.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Wang Shichong executed Zheng Ting and afterward repented, but the order of reprieve arrived too late.

sentences.zh: 今春府史取財不多，朕怒殺之，後亦尋悔，皆由思不審也。

translations.literal: This spring a prefectural clerk took not much property; in anger I killed him, and afterward soon repented—all because reflection was not thorough.
translations.idiomatic: This spring I executed in anger a prefectural clerk who had embezzled a small sum, and soon regretted it. All such errors stem from insufficient deliberation.

sentences.zh: 比來決囚，雖三覆奏，須臾之間，三奏便訖，都未得思，三奏何益？

translations.literal: Recently in deciding prisoners, though there were three re-submissions, within a brief moment the three submissions were finished; there was no chance to reflect at all—what use are three submissions?
translations.idiomatic: Recently, though three re-submissions were required, all three were completed in a moment, leaving no time for reflection. Of what use is such a formality?

sentences.zh: 自今已後，宜二日中五覆奏，下諸州三覆奏。

translations.literal: From now on, within two days there should be five re-submissions; sent down to the prefectures, three re-submissions.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth five re-submissions shall be required over two days in the capital; prefectures shall require three.

sentences.zh: 又古者行刑，君為徹樂減膳。

translations.literal: Moreover, in antiquity when carrying out punishments, the ruler withdrew music and reduced his meals.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in antiquity the ruler withdrew music and reduced his meals on days of execution.

sentences.zh: 朕今庭無常設之樂，莫知何徹，然對食即不啖酒肉。

translations.literal: I now have no music constantly set up in the court and do not know what to withdraw, yet when facing my meal I do not eat wine or meat.
translations.idiomatic: My court has no standing musical establishment, so I know not what to withdraw, yet I abstain from wine and meat at my meals.

sentences.zh: 自今已後，令與尚食相知，刑人日勿進酒肉。

translations.literal: From now on, order the Imperial Kitchen to be informed; on days of execution do not present wine or meat.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the Imperial Kitchen shall be notified, and on days of execution no wine or meat shall be served.

sentences.zh: 內教坊及太常，並宜停教。

translations.literal: The Inner Music Academy and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices should both cease instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The Inner Music Academy and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices shall suspend instruction on such days.

sentences.zh: 且曹司斷獄，多據律文，雖情在可矜，而不敢違法，守文定罪，或恐有冤。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the offices try cases, they mostly rely on the text of the law; though the circumstances may warrant compassion, they do not dare violate the law; adhering to the text in fixing guilt, there may be fear of injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, judicial offices rely chiefly on the letter of the law. Though circumstances may warrant compassion, officials dare not deviate from the statute, and strict adherence to the text may produce injustice.

sentences.zh: 自今門下覆理，有據法合死而情可宥者，宜錄狀奏。

translations.literal: From now on the Chancellery shall review: where according to law one should die but the circumstances may be pardoned, the facts should be recorded and memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the Chancellery shall review cases where the statute requires death but circumstances warrant mercy, recording the facts and memorializing the throne.

sentences.zh: 」自是全活者甚眾。

translations.literal: " From this time those wholly spared were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: " From this time a great many condemned prisoners were spared.

sentences.zh: 其五覆奏，以決前一日、二日覆奏，決日又三覆奏。

translations.literal: The five re-submissions: on the day before the decision and two days before, re-submissions; on the day of decision, three more re-submissions.
translations.idiomatic: The five re-submissions were to be made one and two days before the execution, with three additional submissions on the day of execution.

sentences.zh: 惟犯惡逆者，一覆奏而已，著之於令。

translations.literal: Only for those who committed wicked sedition was one re-submission sufficient; this was written into the ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: Only offenders guilty of wicked sedition required a single re-submission; this was written into the ordinance.

sentences.zh: 太宗既誅張蘊古之後，法官以出罪為誡，時有失入者，又不加罪焉，由是刑網頗密。

translations.literal: After Taizong had executed Zhang Yungu, judges took acquittal as a warning; when there were erroneous convictions, they were not punished either; on this account the net of punishments became rather tight.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Yungu's execution, judges took acquittal as a warning to themselves. Erroneous convictions went unpunished, and the net of justice grew increasingly tight.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問大理卿劉德威曰：「近來刑網稍密，何也？

translations.literal: The emperor once asked Grand Judge Liu Dewei: "Recently the net of punishments has become somewhat tight—why?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked Grand Judge Liu Dewei, "The net of justice has grown tighter of late. Why is this?"

sentences.zh: 」德威對曰：「律文失入減三等，失出減五等。

translations.literal: " Dewei replied: "The text of the law reduces erroneous conviction by three grades and erroneous acquittal by five grades."
translations.idiomatic: " Dewei replied, "The code reduces the penalty for erroneous conviction by three grades and for erroneous acquittal by five grades."

sentences.zh: 今失入則無辜，失出則便獲大罪，所由吏皆深文。

translations.literal: Now if there is erroneous conviction there is no guilt, but if there is erroneous acquittal one immediately receives a great offense; the clerks involved all apply the law with severity.
translations.idiomatic: Today erroneous conviction goes unpunished, while erroneous acquittal incurs severe penalty. Officials therefore apply the law with maximum severity.

sentences.zh: 」太宗然其言。

translations.literal: " Taizong approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong approved his reasoning.

sentences.zh: 由是失於出入者，令依律文，斷獄者漸為平允。

translations.literal: On this account those who erred in acquittal or conviction were ordered to follow the text of the law, and those who tried cases gradually became even and fair.
translations.idiomatic: Judges who erred in acquitting or convicting were thereafter required to follow the statute, and judicial decisions gradually became more equitable.

sentences.zh: 十四年，又制流罪三等，不限以里數，量配邊惡之州。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, they also regulated the three grades of exile, not limiting them by li distance, but assigning according to measure to frontier and harsh prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the three grades of exile were reformed: distance in li was no longer specified; offenders were assigned according to the severity of frontier prefectures.

sentences.zh: 其後雖存寬典，而犯者漸少。

translations.literal: Thereafter, though lenient canons remained, offenders gradually became fewer.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, though lenient laws remained in force, offenders gradually diminished.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，遵貞觀故事，務在恤刑。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne, he followed the precedents of Zhenguan, striving to show compassion in punishments.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong ascended the throne, he followed the Zhenguan precedents and strove to show compassion in the administration of justice.

sentences.zh: 嘗問大理卿唐臨在獄系囚之數，臨對曰：「見囚五十餘人，惟二人合死。

translations.literal: He once asked Grand Judge Tang Lin the number of prisoners detained in the prisons; Lin replied: "Prisoners currently seen are more than fifty persons; only two merit death."
translations.idiomatic: He once asked Grand Judge Tang Lin how many prisoners were detained. Lin replied, "There are somewhat more than fifty prisoners; only two merit the death penalty."

sentences.zh: 」帝以囚數全少，怡然形於顏色。

translations.literal: " The emperor, because the number of prisoners was altogether few, showed contentment in his countenance.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor, pleased that the number of prisoners was so low, showed his satisfaction openly.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，敕太尉長孫無忌、司空李勣、左僕射于志寧、右僕射行成、侍中高季輔、黃門侍郎宇文節柳奭、右丞段寶玄、太常少卿令狐德棻、吏部侍郎高敬言、刑部侍郎劉燕客、給事中趙文恪，中書舍人李友益、少府丞張行實、大理丞元紹、太府丞王文端、刑部郎中賈敏行等，共撰定律令格式。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yonghui, he ordered Grand Preceptor Zhangsun Wuji, Minister of Works Li Ji, Left Vice Director Yu Zhining, Right Vice Director Xing Cheng, Attendant-in-ordinary Gao Jifu, Yellow Gate Vice Directors Yu Wenjie and Liu Shi, Right Assistant Director Duan Baoxuan, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Linghu Defen, Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel Gao Jingyan, Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice Liu Yanke, Attending Gentleman Zhao Wenke, Secretariat Drafter Li Youyi, Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Manufactories Zhang Xingshi, Assistant Grand Judge Yuan Shao, Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Treasury Wang Wenduan, Bureau Director of the Ministry of Justice Jia Minxing, and others jointly to compile and fix statutes, ordinances, regulations, and forms.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yonghui era the emperor charged Grand Preceptor Zhangsun Wuji, Minister of Works Li Ji, Vice Directors Yu Zhining and Xing Cheng, Attendant-in-ordinary Gao Jifu, Vice Directors Yu Wenjie and Liu Shi, Assistant Director Duan Baoxuan, Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices Linghu Defen, Vice Director of Personnel Gao Jingyan, Vice Director of Justice Liu Yanke, Attending Gentleman Zhao Wenke, Secretariat drafter Li Youyi, Assistant Director Zhang Xingshi of the Court of Imperial Manufactories, Assistant Grand Judge Yuan Shao, Assistant Director Wang Wenduan of the Imperial Treasury, Bureau Director Jia Minxing of the Ministry of Justice, and others to compile the statutes, ordinances, regulations, and forms.

sentences.zh: 舊制不便者，皆隨刪改。

translations.literal: Where old institutions were inconvenient, all were deleted and revised as they went.
translations.idiomatic: Provisions of the old code found inconvenient were revised or deleted.

sentences.zh: 遂分格為兩部：曹司常務為《留司格》，天下所共者為《散頒格》。

translations.literal: They then divided the regulations into two parts: routine affairs of the bureaus became the Retained Bureau Regulations; what was shared throughout the realm became the Broadly Promulgated Regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The supplementary regulations were divided into two parts: routine bureau affairs became the Retained Bureau Regulations, and regulations applicable empire-wide became the Broadly Promulgated Regulations.

sentences.zh: 其《散頒格》下州縣，《留司格》但留本司行用焉。

translations.literal: The Broadly Promulgated Regulations were sent down to prefectures and counties; the Retained Bureau Regulations were retained only by the originating offices for use.
translations.idiomatic: The Broadly Promulgated Regulations were distributed to prefectures and counties; the Retained Bureau Regulations were kept by the originating offices for their own use.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔曰：「律學未有定疏，每年所舉明法，遂無憑准。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict said: "Legal studies have no fixed commentary; each year those presented for expertise in law thus have no basis for judgment."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year an edict declared, "Legal studies lack an authoritative commentary, leaving candidates for the legal examinations without a standard of reference."

sentences.zh: 宜廣召解律人條義疏奏聞。

translations.literal: It is fitting broadly to summon those who understand the law to set forth article meanings in commentary and memorialize for the throne's knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: Let scholars versed in the law be summoned to prepare commentaries on each article and submit them for imperial review.

sentences.zh: 仍使中書、門下監定。

translations.literal: They were also to have the Secretariat and Chancellery supervise and fix them.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat and Chancellery were charged with supervising and approving the work.

sentences.zh: 」於是太尉趙國公無忌、司空英國公勣、尚書左僕射兼太子少師監修國史燕國公志寧、銀青光祿大夫刑部尚書唐臨、太中大夫守大理卿段寶玄、朝議大夫守尚書右丞劉燕客、朝議大夫守御史中丞賈敏行等，參撰《律疏》，成三十卷，四年十月奏之，頒於天下。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Grand Preceptor Zhao, Duke of Zhao, Wuji; Minister of Works Li, Duke of Ying, Ji; Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and Junior Preceptor to the Crown Prince, supervising the compilation of the national history, Yan, Duke of Yan, Zhining; Grand Master of Brilliant Happiness with Silver Seal, Minister of Justice Tang Lin; Grand Master Duan Baoxuan, acting Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review; Gentleman for Discussing Affairs Liu Yanke, acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat; Gentleman for Discussing Affairs Jia Minxing, acting Vice Censor-in-Chief; and others jointly compiled the Statutory Commentary, completing thirty scrolls; in the tenth month of the fourth year they submitted it, and it was promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Wuji, Duke of Zhao and Grand Preceptor; Li Ji, Duke of Ying and Minister of Works; Xu Zhining, Duke of Yan, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and supervisor of the national history; Tang Lin, Minister of Justice; Duan Baoxuan, Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review; Liu Yanke, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat; Jia Minxing, Vice Censor-in-Chief; and others jointly drafted the Statutory Commentary in thirty scrolls, submitted it in the tenth month of the fourth year, and had it promulgated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 自是斷獄者皆引疏分析之。

translations.literal: From then on, those who decided cases all cited the commentary to analyze them.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, all who adjudicated cases cited the commentary in their analysis.

sentences.zh: 永徽五年五月，上謂侍臣曰：「獄訟繁多，皆由刑罰枉濫，故曰刑者成也，一成而不可變。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year of Yonghui, the emperor said to his attendants: "Prison cases and lawsuits are numerous, all because punishments are wrongly applied; hence it is said that punishment means completion—once fixed it must not be changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year of Yonghui, the emperor told his ministers: "Prison cases and lawsuits abound, all because punishments are misapplied. As the saying goes, punishment means a settled judgment—once rendered, it must not be altered.

sentences.zh: 末代斷獄之人，皆以苛刻為明，是以秦氏網密秋荼，而獲罪者眾。

translations.literal: Those who decided cases in later ages all took harsh severity as clarity; hence the Qin dynasty's nets were dense as autumn bitter herb, and those who incurred guilt were many.
translations.idiomatic: In later ages, judges took harshness for clarity; thus the Qin wove its laws tight as autumn bitter herb, and multitudes were condemned.

sentences.zh: 今天下無事，四海乂安，欲與公等共行寬政。

translations.literal: Now the realm is at peace and the four seas tranquil; I wish to practice lenient governance together with you.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the realm is untroubled and the four seas at peace, I wish to join you in practicing lenient governance.

sentences.zh: 今日刑罰，得無枉濫乎？

translations.literal: Today's punishments—are they not wrongly applied?
translations.idiomatic: Are there no wrongful applications in today's punishments?

sentences.zh: 」無忌對曰：「陛下欲得刑法寬平，臣下猶不識聖意。

translations.literal: " Wuji replied: "Your Majesty wishes to have the penal code lenient and equitable, yet your subjects still do not understand the sage intent.
translations.idiomatic: " Wuji answered: "Your Majesty wishes the penal code to be lenient and fair, yet your officials still fail to grasp your intent.

sentences.zh: 此法弊來已久，非止今日。

translations.literal: These evils in the law have long persisted; they did not begin only today.
translations.idiomatic: These abuses of the law have persisted for a long time; they did not begin only today.

sentences.zh: 若情在體國，即共號癡人，意在深文，便稱好吏。

translations.literal: If one's feeling lay in serving the state, together they would call one a fool; if one's intent lay in strict textual construction of charges, one was called a good official.
translations.idiomatic: If one sought the welfare of the state, all would call him a fool; if one pursued harsh textual penalties, he was hailed as a capable official.

sentences.zh: 所以罪雖合杖，必欲遣徒，理有可生，務入於死，非憎前人，陷於死刑。

translations.literal: Therefore though the offense warranted the cudgel, they would insist on banishment; though reason allowed life, they strove to put one to death—not from hatred of the person, but to ensnare him in the death penalty.
