translations.idiomatic: Thus though an offense merited beating, they would push for penal servitude; though logic allowed sparing a life, they pressed for death—not from personal hatred, but to trap the accused in a capital sentence.

sentences.zh: 陛下矜而令放，法司亦宜固請，但陛下喜怒不妄加於人，刑罰自然適中。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty pities and orders release, the law officers ought likewise to press their petitions firmly; only if Your Majesty does not capriciously impose joy or anger upon people will punishments naturally become fitting.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty shows mercy and orders release, the courts should press their petitions as well; if Your Majesty does not capriciously vent favor or wrath upon others, punishments will naturally be balanced.

sentences.zh: 」上以為然。

translations.literal: " The emperor considered this correct.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 永徽六年七月，上謂侍臣曰：「律通比附，條例太多。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year of Yonghui, the emperor said to his attendants: "The statutes rely extensively on analogical application, and the articles are too numerous.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the sixth year of Yonghui, the emperor told his ministers: "The statutes rely too heavily on analogical application, and the articles are too numerous.

sentences.zh: 」左僕射志寧等對：「舊律多比附斷事，乃稍難解。

translations.literal: " Left Vice Director Zhining and others replied: "The old statutes relied much on analogical judgment in deciding cases, which was somewhat hard to understand.
translations.idiomatic: " Left Vice Director Zhining and others answered: "The old statutes relied heavily on analogical judgment, which made cases somewhat difficult to understand.

sentences.zh: 科條極眾，數至三千。

translations.literal: The statutory articles were extremely numerous, reaching three thousand in count.
translations.idiomatic: The statutory articles were extremely numerous, numbering as many as three thousand.

sentences.zh: 隋日再定，惟留五百。

translations.literal: The Sui daily revised and fixed them again, retaining only five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui they were revised again, leaving only five hundred articles.

sentences.zh: 以事類相似者，比附科斷。

translations.literal: Similar matters were punished by analogical application of articles.
translations.idiomatic: Similar cases were adjudicated by analogical application of the relevant articles.

sentences.zh: 今日所停，即是參取隋律修易。

translations.literal: What stops today is precisely taking the Sui statutes as reference for revision.
translations.idiomatic: The code now in force was revised with reference to the Sui statutes.

sentences.zh: 條章既少，極成省便。」

translations.literal: Since the articles and chapters are few, they are extremely convenient and economical."
translations.idiomatic: With so few articles and chapters, the code is far more convenient and economical."

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改易官號，因敕司刑太常伯源直心、少常伯李敬玄、司刑大夫李文禮等重定格式，惟改曹局之名，而不易篇第。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo, when official titles were changed, an edict ordered Director of Penal Affairs Yuan Zhixin, Vice Director Li Jingxuan, Grand Master of Penal Affairs Li Wenli, and others to re-fix the regulations and forms, changing only the names of bureaus without altering the sequence of chapters.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Longshuo, when official titles were changed, an edict directed Yuan Zhixin, Director of Penal Affairs, Li Jingxuan, Vice Director, Li Wenli, Grand Master of Penal Affairs, and others to revise the regulations and forms, changing only bureau names while leaving the chapter sequence intact.

sentences.zh: 麟德二年奏上。

translations.literal: In the second year of Linde it was submitted.
translations.idiomatic: It was submitted in the second year of Linde.

sentences.zh: 至儀鳳中，官號復舊，又敕左僕射劉仁軌、右僕射戴至德、侍中張文瓘、中書令李敬玄、右庶子郝處俊、黃門侍郎來恆、左庶子高智周、右庶子李義琰、吏部侍郎裴行儉馬載、兵部侍郎蕭德昭裴炎、工部侍郎李義琛、刑部侍郎張楚、金部郎中盧律師等，刪緝格式。

translations.literal: By the Yifeng era, when official titles were restored, another edict ordered Left Vice Director Liu Rengui, Right Vice Director Dai Zhide, Palace Attendant Zhang Wenguan, Grand Counselor Li Jingxuan, Right Attendant of the Heir Apparent Hao Chujun, Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Lai Heng, Left Attendant Gao Zhizhou, Right Attendant Li Yiyan, Vice Director of Personnel Pei Xingjian and Ma Zai, Vice Director of War Xiao Dezhao and Pei Yan, Vice Director of Works Li Yichen, Vice Director of Justice Zhang Chu, and Section Director of Treasury Lu Lüshi, among others, to delete and compile the regulations and forms.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yifeng era, when official titles were restored, another edict charged Liu Rengui, Left Vice Director; Dai Zhide, Right Vice Director; Zhang Wenguan, Palace Attendant; Li Jingxuan, Grand Counselor; Hao Chujun and Li Yiyan, Attendants of the Heir Apparent; Lai Heng, Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat; Gao Zhizhou, Left Attendant of the Heir Apparent; Pei Xingjian and Ma Zai, Vice Directors of Personnel; Xiao Dezhao and Pei Yan, Vice Directors of War; Li Yichen, Vice Director of Works; Zhang Chu, Vice Director of Justice; Lu Lüshi, Section Director of the Treasury; and others with revising and compiling the regulations and forms.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳二年二月九日，撰定奏上。

translations.literal: On the ninth day of the second month of the second year of Yifeng, the compilation was completed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth day of the second month of the second year of Yifeng, the revised code was completed and submitted.

sentences.zh: 先是詳刑少卿趙仁本撰《法例》三卷，引以斷獄，時議亦為折衷。

translations.literal: Earlier, Vice Director of Detailed Punishments Zhao Renben compiled three scrolls of Legal Precedents, citing them to decide cases; contemporary opinion also regarded this as a balanced approach.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhao Renben, Vice Director of Detailed Punishments, had compiled three scrolls of Legal Precedents for use in adjudication, and contemporary opinion regarded the work as a reasonable compromise.

sentences.zh: 後高宗覽之，以為煩文不便。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Gaozong reviewed it and considered the verbose text inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Emperor Gaozong reviewed it, he found the verbose text cumbersome.

sentences.zh: 因謂侍臣曰：「律、令、格、式，天下通規，非朕庸虛所能創制。

translations.literal: He therefore said to his attendants: "Statutes, commands, supplementary regulations, and forms are universal norms of the realm—not something this mediocre and empty sovereign could create.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore told his ministers: "Statutes, commands, supplementary regulations, and forms are the universal norms of the realm—not something a sovereign as mediocre as I could devise.

sentences.zh: 並是武德之際，貞觀已來，或取定宸衷，參詳眾議，條章備舉，軌躅昭然，臨事遵行，自不能盡。

translations.literal: All were fixed during the Wude era and since the Zhenguan period—sometimes settled by the imperial heart, sometimes deliberated among the assembled; the articles were fully set forth and the tracks clearly marked; in acting on affairs one follows them and naturally cannot exhaust them all.
translations.idiomatic: All were established during the Wude era and refined since Zhenguan—sometimes settled by imperial decision, sometimes shaped through collective deliberation. The articles were fully set forth and the standards clearly marked; in practice one follows them and can scarcely exhaust their scope.

sentences.zh: 何為更須作例，致使觸緒多疑。

translations.literal: Why must one further compose precedents, causing one to touch every thread with many doubts?
translations.idiomatic: Why must we compose further precedents, only to breed doubt at every turn?

sentences.zh: 計此因循，非適今日，速宜改轍，不得更然。

translations.literal: I reckon this inertia is not limited to today; the course should quickly be changed and must not continue thus.
translations.idiomatic: This inertia is nothing new; the course must be changed at once and must not continue.

sentences.zh: 」自是，《法例》遂廢不用。

translations.literal: " From then on, the Legal Precedents were abandoned and no longer used.
translations.idiomatic: " From that point the Legal Precedents were abandoned and no longer used.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，初欲大收人望。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu assumed the regency, at first she wished greatly to win popular esteem.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu assumed the regency, she initially sought to win broad popular support.

sentences.zh: 垂拱初年，令熔銅為匭，四面置門，各依方色，共為一室。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chuigong, she ordered copper cast into boxes; on four sides doors were placed, each according to its directional color, together forming one chamber.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chuigong, she ordered copper cast into suggestion boxes with doors on all four sides, each painted according to its directional color, together forming one chamber.

sentences.zh: 東面名曰延恩匭，上賦頌及許求官爵者封表投之。

translations.literal: The eastern side was called the Box for Extending Grace; those submitting encomia or petitions seeking offices and ranks sealed memorials and cast them in.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern side was called the Box for Extending Grace; those submitting encomia or petitions for office and rank sealed their memorials and deposited them there.

sentences.zh: 南面曰招諫匭，有言時政得失及直言諫諍者投之。

translations.literal: The southern side was called the Box for Soliciting Remonstrance; those who had words on the gains and losses of current policy or direct remonstrance cast them in.
translations.idiomatic: The southern side was called the Box for Soliciting Remonstrance; those wishing to speak on the merits and failings of current policy or to remonstrate directly deposited their submissions there.

sentences.zh: 西面曰申冤匭，有得罪冤濫者投之。

translations.literal: The western side was called the Box for Stating Grievances; those wrongly condemned cast them in.
translations.idiomatic: The western side was called the Box for Stating Grievances; those who had suffered wrongful conviction deposited their petitions there.

sentences.zh: 北面曰通玄匭，有玄象災變及軍謀秘策者投之。

translations.literal: The northern side was called the Box for Communicating Mysteries; those with celestial omens, calamities, or secret military stratagems cast them in.
translations.idiomatic: The northern side was called the Box for Communicating Mysteries; those reporting celestial omens, natural disasters, or secret military plans deposited their submissions there.

sentences.zh: 每日置之於朝堂，以收天下表疏。

translations.literal: Each day they were placed in the court hall to receive memorials from throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Each day the boxes were set out in the court hall to receive memorials from across the realm.

sentences.zh: 既出之後，不逞之徒，或至攻訐陰私，謗訕朝政者。

translations.literal: After they were put out, unscrupulous persons sometimes even attacked private matters, slandering court policy.
translations.idiomatic: Once the boxes were in place, unscrupulous persons sometimes used them to attack private matters and slander court policy.

sentences.zh: 後乃令中書、門下官一人，專監其所投之狀，仍責識官，然後許進封，行之至今焉。

translations.literal: Later one official each from the Secretariat and Chancellery was assigned exclusively to supervise the petitions cast in; officials were still required to identify themselves, and only then was sealed submission permitted—a practice carried on to the present.
translations.idiomatic: Later one official each from the Secretariat and Chancellery was assigned to supervise submissions; petitioners were still required to identify themselves, and only then was sealed submission permitted—a practice that continues to the present.

sentences.zh: 則天又敕內史裴居道、夏官尚書岑長倩、鳳閣侍郎韋方質與刪定官袁智弘等十餘人，刪改格式，加計帳及勾帳式，通舊式成二十卷。

translations.literal: Empress Wu also ordered Grand Counselor Pei Judao, Minister of the Summer Office Cen Changqian, Vice Director of the Phoenix Pavilion Wei Fangzhi, and more than ten revision officials including Yuan Zhihong to delete and revise the regulations and forms, adding accounting and audit forms; together with the old forms they amounted to twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu also ordered Pei Judao, Grand Counselor; Cen Changqian, Minister of the Summer Office; Wei Fangzhi, Vice Director of the Phoenix Pavilion; and more than ten revision officials including Yuan Zhihong to revise the regulations and forms, adding accounting and audit forms; together with the old forms, the result was twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 又以武德已來、垂拱已前詔敕便於時者，編為《新格》二卷，則天自製序。

translations.literal: She also took edicts and orders from the Wude era onward through before Chuigong that were convenient for the times and compiled them into two scrolls of New Supplementary Regulations, with a preface written by Empress Wu herself.
translations.idiomatic: She also compiled edicts and orders from the Wude era through the period before Chuigong that remained useful into two scrolls of New Supplementary Regulations, for which Empress Wu herself wrote the preface.

sentences.zh: 其二卷之外，別編六卷，堪為當司行用，為《垂拱留司格》。

translations.literal: Beyond these two scrolls, six scrolls were separately compiled, suitable for use by the respective offices, titled the Chuigong Retained Bureau Regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond these two scrolls, six more were separately compiled for use by the respective offices, titled the Chuigong Retained Bureau Regulations.

sentences.zh: 時韋方質詳練法理，又委其事于咸陽尉王守慎，又有經理之才，故《垂拱格》、《式》，議者稱為詳密。

translations.literal: At the time Wei Fangzhi was thoroughly versed in legal principles, and he also entrusted the matter to Commandant of Xianyang Wang Shouzhen, who also had talent for managing affairs; hence the Chuigong Regulations and Forms were praised by commentators as thorough and meticulous.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wei Fangzhi was thoroughly versed in legal principles and entrusted the work to Wang Shouzhen, Commandant of Xianyang, who also had a gift for administration; commentators therefore praised the Chuigong Regulations and Forms as thorough and meticulous.

sentences.zh: 其律令惟改二十四條，又有不便者，大抵依舊。

translations.literal: Of the statutes and commands, only twenty-four articles were changed; where there were still inconveniences, they largely followed the old pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Of the statutes and commands, only twenty-four articles were revised; where difficulties remained, the old provisions were largely retained.

sentences.zh: 然則天嚴于用刑，屬徐敬業作亂，及豫、博兵起之後，恐人心動搖，欲以威制天下，漸引酷吏，務令深文，以案刑獄。

translations.literal: Yet Empress Wu was strict in applying punishments; when Xu Jingye raised rebellion and after troops rose in Yu and Bo, fearing hearts would waver, she wished to control the realm by awe and gradually employed cruel officials, striving for strict textual construction to investigate criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Empress Wu was severe in applying punishments. After Xu Jingye's rebellion and the uprisings in Yu and Bo, fearing popular unrest, she sought to control the realm through terror and gradually brought in cruel officials, pressing for harsh textual penalties in criminal investigations.

sentences.zh: 長壽年有上封事言嶺表流人有陰謀逆者，乃遣司刑評事萬國俊攝監察御史就案之，若得反狀，斬決。

translations.literal: In the Changshou era a sealed memorial reported that exiles in the Ling region were secretly plotting rebellion; she sent Penal Affairs Assessor Wan Guojun, acting as Investigating Censor, to investigate on the spot; if evidence of rebellion was obtained, they were to be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: In the Changshou era a sealed memorial reported that exiles in the Ling region were secretly plotting rebellion. She sent Wan Guojun, a Penal Affairs Assessor acting as Investigating Censor, to investigate on the spot, with orders to behead any who showed evidence of treason.

sentences.zh: 國俊至廣州，遍召流人，擁之水曲，以次加戮。

translations.literal: Guojun reached Guangzhou, summoned all exiles, drove them to the water's edge, and executed them one by one.
translations.idiomatic: Guojun reached Guangzhou, summoned all the exiles, drove them to the water's edge, and executed them one by one.

sentences.zh: 三百餘人，一時並命，然後鍛煉曲成反狀。

translations.literal: More than three hundred persons were killed at once; only afterward were confessions of rebellion forged through torture.
translations.idiomatic: More than three hundred were killed at once; only afterward were confessions of rebellion forged through torture.

sentences.zh: 乃更誣奏云：「諸道流人，多有怨望。

translations.literal: He then further submitted a false memorial saying: "Exiles in various circuits mostly harbor resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a false memorial stating: "Exiles in various circuits mostly harbor resentment.

sentences.zh: 若不推究，為變不遙。

translations.literal: If not investigated thoroughly, rebellion is not far off.
translations.idiomatic: Unless thoroughly investigated, rebellion will not be far off.

sentences.zh: 」則天深然其言。

translations.literal: " Empress Wu deeply approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: " Empress Wu strongly approved his report.

sentences.zh: 又命攝監察御史劉光業、王德壽、鮑思恭、王處貞、屈貞筠等，分往劍南、黔中、安南、嶺南等六道，按鞫流人。

translations.literal: She also ordered acting Investigating Censors Liu Guangye, Wang Deshou, Bao Sigong, Wang Chuzhen, Qu Zhenyun, and others to separate and go to the six circuits of Jiannan, Qianzhong, Annam, Lingnan, and others to investigate and interrogate exiles.
translations.idiomatic: She also ordered Liu Guangye, Wang Deshou, Bao Sigong, Wang Chuzhen, Qu Zhenyun, and others, acting as Investigating Censors, to divide among the six circuits of Jiannan, Qianzhong, Annam, Lingnan, and elsewhere to investigate and interrogate exiles.

sentences.zh: 光業所在殺戮。

translations.literal: Where Guangye went, he slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Guangye went, he slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 光業誅九百人，德壽誅七百人，其餘少者不減數百人。

translations.literal: Guangye executed nine hundred, Deshou seven hundred; the rest, though fewer, were no less than several hundred each.
translations.idiomatic: Guangye executed nine hundred, Deshou seven hundred, and the others, though fewer, still killed no less than several hundred each.

sentences.zh: 亦有雜犯及遠年流人，亦枉及禍焉。

translations.literal: There were also miscellaneous offenders and exiles from years past who were wrongly swept into disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous offenders and exiles from years past were also wrongly swept up in the slaughter.

sentences.zh: 時周興、來俊臣等，相次受制推究大獄。

translations.literal: At the time Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and others successively received orders to investigate major cases.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and others were successively ordered to investigate major cases.

sentences.zh: 乃于都城麗景門內，別置推事使院，時人謂之「新開獄」。

translations.literal: They set up a separate Office of Investigation Commissioners inside Lijing Gate in the capital; people of the time called it the "Newly Opened Prison."
translations.idiomatic: They established a separate Office of Investigation Commissioners inside Lijing Gate in the capital, which people of the time called the "Newly Opened Prison."

sentences.zh: 俊臣又與侍御史侯思止王弘義郭霸李敬仁、評事康暐衛遂忠等，招集告事數百人，共為羅織，以陷良善。

translations.literal: Junchen also, with Attending Censor Hou Sizhi, Wang Hongyi, Guo Ba, Li Jingren, and Assessors Kang Wei and Wei Suizhong, recruited several hundred informants to weave false charges together and entrap the innocent.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen also joined with the Attending Censors Hou Sizhi, Wang Hongyi, Guo Ba, and Li Jingren and the Assessors Kang Wei and Wei Suizhong to recruit several hundred informants, who together fabricated charges to entrap the innocent.

sentences.zh: 前後枉遭殺害者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Those wrongly killed before and after were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Those wrongly killed in this way were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 又造《告密羅織經》一卷，其意旨皆網羅前人，織成反狀。

translations.literal: He also composed one scroll of the Manual for Informing and Fabricating Charges; its purport was entirely to ensnare the accused and weave rebellion confessions.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled a one-scroll Manual for Informing and Fabricating Charges, whose whole purpose was to ensnare the accused and weave confessions of treason.

sentences.zh: 俊臣每鞫囚，無問輕重，多以醋灌鼻。

translations.literal: Whenever Junchen interrogated prisoners, regardless of severity, he often poured vinegar into their nostrils.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Junchen interrogated prisoners, regardless of the severity of the offense, he often poured vinegar into their nostrils.

sentences.zh: 禁地牢中，或盛之於甕，以火圍繞炙之。

translations.literal: In underground dungeons he sometimes placed them in jars and roasted them with fire all around.
translations.idiomatic: In underground dungeons he sometimes placed them in jars and roasted them with fire all around.

sentences.zh: 兼絕其糧餉，至有抽衣絮以啖之者。

translations.literal: He also cut off their rations, until some stripped wadding from clothing to eat.
translations.idiomatic: He also cut off their rations, until some were reduced to stripping wadding from their clothing to eat.

sentences.zh: 其所作大枷，凡有十號：一曰定百脈，二曰喘不得，三曰突地吼，四曰著即承，五曰失魂膽，六曰實同反，七曰反是實，八曰死豬愁，九曰求即死，十曰求破家。

translations.literal: The great cangues he made numbered ten in all: first, Fixing the Hundred Vessels; second, Cannot Breathe; third, Earth-Shaking Roar; fourth, Put It On and Confess; fifth, Lost Soul and Gall; sixth, Truth Is Rebellion; seventh, Rebellion Is Truth; eighth, Dead Pig's Distress; ninth, Seek Immediate Death; tenth, Seek Ruin of the Family.
translations.idiomatic: The great cangues he devised numbered ten in all: Fixing the Hundred Vessels; Cannot Breathe; Earth-Shaking Roar; Put It On and Confess; Lost Soul and Gall; Truth Is Rebellion; Rebellion Is Truth; Dead Pig's Distress; Seek Immediate Death; and Seek Ruin of the Family.

sentences.zh: 又令寢處糞穢，備諸苦毒。

translations.literal: He also made them sleep amid filth, applying every bitter torment.
translations.idiomatic: He also made them sleep amid filth and subjected them to every form of torment.

sentences.zh: 每有制書寬宥囚徒，俊臣必先遣獄卒，盡殺重罪，然後宣示。

translations.literal: Whenever an imperial edict pardoned prisoners, Junchen would first send jailers to kill all those guilty of serious crimes, and only then announce the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an imperial edict pardoned prisoners, Junchen would first send jailers to kill all those convicted of serious crimes, and only then announce the edict.

sentences.zh: 是時海內懾懼，道路以目。

translations.literal: At that time the realm within the seas was fear-stricken; people on the roads dared only exchange glances.
translations.idiomatic: At that time terror gripped the realm; on the roads people dared only exchange glances in silence.

sentences.zh: 麟台正字陳子昂上書曰：

translations.literal: Chen Zi'ang, Rectifier of the Archives, submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zi'ang, Rectifier of the Archives, submitted a memorial stating:

sentences.zh: 臣聞古之禦天下者，其政有三：王者化之，用仁義也；

translations.literal: I have heard that those who governed the realm in antiquity had three policies: kings transformed it, employing benevolence and righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that those who governed the realm in antiquity pursued three policies: kings transformed it through benevolence and righteousness;

sentences.zh: 霸者威之，任權智也；

translations.literal: hegemons awed it, relying on authority and craft;
translations.idiomatic: hegemons awed it through authority and stratagem;

sentences.zh: 強國脅之，務刑罰也。

translations.literal: powerful states coerced it, focusing on punishments.
translations.idiomatic: powerful states coerced it through punishments.

sentences.zh: 是以化之不足，然後威之，威之不足，然後刑之。

translations.literal: Therefore when transformation was insufficient, then they awed; when awe was insufficient, then they punished.
translations.idiomatic: When transformation proved insufficient, they turned to awe; when awe proved insufficient, they turned to punishment.

sentences.zh: 故至於刑，則非王者之所貴矣。

translations.literal: Thus when it came to punishment, that was not what kings prized.
translations.idiomatic: Thus punishment was not what true kings valued.

sentences.zh: 況欲光宅天下，追功上皇，專任刑殺以為威斷，可謂策之失者也。

translations.literal: How much more so—wishing to illuminate and settle the realm, matching the achievements of the August Ancestor, yet relying exclusively on killing as the instrument of awe—this may be called a failure of policy.
translations.idiomatic: How much less fitting, then, to seek to illuminate and settle the realm and match the achievements of the August Ancestor, yet rely exclusively on killing as the instrument of authority—this may be called a failure of policy.

sentences.zh: 臣伏睹陛下聖德聰明，遊心太古，將制靜宇宙，保乂黎民，發號施令，出於誠慊。

translations.literal: I humbly behold Your Majesty's sage virtue and intelligence, your heart roaming in high antiquity, about to settle the cosmos in tranquility and protect the people, issuing commands from sincere purpose.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly behold Your Majesty's sage virtue and intelligence, your heart set on the ways of high antiquity, intent on settling the cosmos in tranquility and protecting the people, issuing commands from sincere conviction.

sentences.zh: 天下蒼生，莫不懸望聖風，冀見神化，道德為政，將侍于陛下矣。

translations.literal: All the common people under heaven none fail to look up to the sage wind, hoping to witness divine transformation; rule by virtue awaits Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: All the people under heaven look up to your sage influence, hoping to witness divine transformation; rule by virtue awaits Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 臣聞之，聖人出，必有驅除，蓋天人之符，應休命也。

translations.literal: I have heard that when a sage appears, there must be purging—it is the accord of Heaven and man, responding to glorious destiny.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when a sage appears, purging must follow—it is the accord of Heaven and man, responding to a glorious destiny.

sentences.zh: 日者東南微孽，敢謀亂常。

translations.literal: Recently a petty rebel band in the southeast dared to plot disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Recently a petty rebel band in the southeast dared to plot rebellion.

sentences.zh: 陛下順天行誅，罪惡咸伏，豈非天意欲彰陛下威武之功哉！

translations.literal: Your Majesty followed Heaven in executing punishment; all guilt was subdued—is this not Heaven's intent to display Your Majesty's martial power and merit!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty followed Heaven in executing punishment, and all guilt was subdued—is this not Heaven's intent to display your martial power and merit!

sentences.zh: 而執事者不察天心，以為人意，惡其首亂唱禍，法合誅屠，將息奸源，窮其黨與。

translations.literal: Yet those in charge did not discern Heaven's heart, taking it for human will; they hated the ringleaders who stirred rebellion and spread calamity; the law warranted execution; they wished to still the source of treachery and exhaust their factions.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those in charge failed to discern Heaven's intent, treating it as mere human will; they hated the ringleaders who stirred rebellion and spread calamity, held that the law warranted execution, and sought to still the source of treachery and exhaust their factions.

sentences.zh: 遂使陛下大開詔獄，重設嚴刑，冀以懲奸，觀於天下。

translations.literal: Thus they caused Your Majesty to open wide the edict-prisons, re-establish harsh punishments, hoping to punish treachery and display this to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they caused Your Majesty to open wide the edict-prisons, reimpose harsh punishments, and display stern retribution to the realm.

sentences.zh: 逆党親屬及其交遊，有涉嫌疑，辭相連及，莫不窮捕考校，枝葉蟠拿。

translations.literal: Relatives of rebels and their associates, whenever suspicion attached or testimony linked them, were all hunted to the end, examined and tortured; branches and leaves were seized in coils.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives of rebels and their associates, whenever suspicion attached or testimony linked them, were hunted to the end, examined and tortured; every branch and leaf of the conspiracy was seized.

sentences.zh: 大或流血，小禦魑魅。

translations.literal: In major cases blood flowed; in minor ones they were condemned as though to ward off demon sprites.
translations.idiomatic: In major cases blood was shed; in minor ones the condemned were punished as though to subdue demonic spirits.

sentences.zh: 至有奸人熒惑，乘險相誣，糾告疑似，冀圖爵賞，叫于闕下者，日有數矣。

translations.literal: Even wicked men, deluding others, seized opportunities to accuse one another, reporting suspected cases hoping for ranks and rewards; those crying out at the palace gates numbered several each day.
translations.idiomatic: Wicked men, deluding others, seized opportunities to accuse one another, reporting suspected cases in hopes of rank and reward; several such petitioners cried out at the palace gates each day.

sentences.zh: 于時朝廷徨徨，莫能自固，海內傾聽，以相驚恐。

translations.literal: At that time the court was restless and could not secure itself; within the seas all listened with dread, mutually frightening one another.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court was restless and could not secure itself; throughout the realm all listened in dread, frightening one another.

sentences.zh: 賴陛下仁慈，憫其危懼，賜以恩詔，許其大功已上，一切勿論。

translations.literal: Thanks to Your Majesty's benevolence, pitying their terror, you granted a gracious edict, providing that for connections no closer than the great-merit mourning grade, nothing would be prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Your Majesty's benevolence and pity for their terror, you granted a gracious edict providing that all whose complicity fell short of the closest conspiracy—including even distant kinship ties—would go unpunished.

sentences.zh: 人時獲泰，謂生再造。

translations.literal: People at the time attained peace and called it a second birth.
translations.idiomatic: People at the time found relief and spoke of being given life anew.

sentences.zh: 愚臣竊以忻然，賀陛下聖明，得天之機也。

translations.literal: This foolish subject inwardly rejoiced, congratulating Your Majesty's sage clarity in seizing Heaven's opportune moment.
translations.idiomatic: This foolish subject inwardly rejoiced, congratulating Your Majesty on your sage clarity in seizing Heaven's opportune moment.

sentences.zh: 不謂議者異見，又執前圖，比者刑獄，紛紛復起。

translations.literal: I did not expect dissenting views among counsellors, clutching again to the former course; lately criminal cases have risen in tumult once more.
translations.idiomatic: I did not expect counsellors with dissenting views to cling again to the former course; lately criminal cases have proliferated once more.

sentences.zh: 陛下不深思天意，以順休期，尚以督察為理，威刑為務，使前者之詔，不信於人。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has not deeply pondered Heaven's intent to align with this glorious season, but still takes investigation as governance and awe through punishment as the task, causing the former edict not to be trusted among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has not deeply pondered Heaven's intent in this glorious season, but still takes investigation as governance and terror through punishment as the task, causing the former edict to lose credibility among the people.

sentences.zh: 愚臣昧焉，竊恐非五帝、三王伐罪吊人之意也。

translations.literal: This foolish subject is blind, and I secretly fear this is not the intent of the Five Emperors and Three Kings in punishing guilt and comforting the people.
translations.idiomatic: This foolish subject is blind, and I secretly fear this is not the intent of the Five Emperors and Three Kings in punishing the guilty and comforting the people.

sentences.zh: 臣竊觀當今天下百姓，思安久矣。

translations.literal: I secretly observe that the common people under heaven today have long yearned for peace.
translations.idiomatic: I secretly observe that the people of the realm today have long yearned for peace.

sentences.zh: 曩屬北胡侵塞，西戎寇邊，兵革相屠，向曆十載。

translations.literal: Formerly they suffered northern barbarians invading the passes and western tribes raiding the borders; arms slaughtered one another for nearly ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly they suffered northern barbarians invading the frontier and western tribes raiding the borders; war consumed them for nearly ten years.

sentences.zh: 關、河自北，轉輸幽、燕；

translations.literal: From Tong and the Yellow River northward, transport worked toward You and Yan;
translations.idiomatic: From Tong Pass and the Yellow River northward, transport lines ran toward You and Yan;

sentences.zh: 秦、蜀之西，馳騖湟、海。

translations.literal: west of Qin and Shu, horses raced toward Huang and the sea.
translations.idiomatic: west of Qin and Shu, supply lines raced toward the Huangshui and the western sea.

sentences.zh: 當時天下疲極矣！

translations.literal: At that time the realm was utterly exhausted!
translations.idiomatic: At that time the realm was utterly exhausted!

sentences.zh: 重以大兵之後，屬遭凶年，流離饑餓，死喪略半。

translations.literal: Compounded by great armies afterward, they then met famine years; wandering in exile and starving, the dead and lost were nearly half.
translations.idiomatic: Compounded by the aftermath of great armies, they then suffered famine years; wandering in exile and starvation, nearly half the people died or were lost.

sentences.zh: 幸賴陛下以至聖之德，撫寧兆人，邊境獲安，中國無事，陰陽大順，年穀累登，天下父子，始得相養矣。

translations.literal: Fortunately relying on Your Majesty's supreme sage virtue, comforting and settling the myriad people, the borders were secured, the central land untroubled, yin and yang greatly accorded, harvests year after year abundant—the fathers and sons of the realm at last could sustain one another.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately, through Your Majesty's supreme sage virtue in comforting and settling the myriad people, the borders were secured, the central provinces untroubled, yin and yang greatly accorded, and harvests abundant year after year—the fathers and sons of the realm at last could sustain one another.

sentences.zh: 揚州構禍，殆有五旬，而海中晏然，纖塵不動，豈非天下蒸庶厭凶亂哉？

translations.literal: When Yangzhou stirred calamity, it lasted nearly fifty days, yet within the seas all was calm, not a speck stirred—is this not because the masses of the realm loathe violent disorder?
translations.idiomatic: When Yangzhou stirred rebellion, it lasted nearly fifty days, yet the realm remained calm and undisturbed—is this not because the people loathe violent disorder?

sentences.zh: 臣以此卜之，百姓思安久矣。

translations.literal: By this I divined it: the common people have long yearned for peace.
translations.idiomatic: From this I infer that the people have long yearned for peace.

sentences.zh: 今陛下不務玄默，以救疲民，而又任威刑以失其望，欲以察察為政，肅理寰區。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty does not practice profound stillness to succor the weary people, yet again relies on stern punishments and thereby loses their hope, wishing to govern with harsh scrutiny and sternly order the whole realm.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty does not practice quiet governance to relieve a weary people, yet again relies on harsh punishments and thereby forfeits their trust, aiming to rule through relentless scrutiny and impose stern order across the realm.

sentences.zh: 愚臣暗昧，竊有大惑。

translations.literal: Your foolish minister is dim and muddled; I privately harbor great perplexity.
translations.idiomatic: Your humble servant is dull of mind and privately greatly perplexed.

sentences.zh: 且臣聞刑者，政之末節也。

translations.literal: Moreover I have heard that punishments are the outermost measure of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, I have heard that punishment is the last resort of governance.

sentences.zh: 先王以禁暴厘亂，不得已而用之。

translations.literal: Former kings used them to restrain violence and set right disorder, employing them only when they had no choice.
translations.idiomatic: Former kings wielded them only to restrain violence and set disorder aright, turning to them when they had no choice.

sentences.zh: 今天下幸安，萬物思泰，陛下乃以末節之法，察理平人，愚臣以為非適變隨時之義也。

translations.literal: Now the realm is fortunately at peace and all things yearn for tranquility, yet Your Majesty applies measures meant as last resorts to scrutinize and judge ordinary people—your foolish minister believes this is not the principle of adapting to change according to the times.
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is fortunately at peace and all things yearn for tranquility, yet Your Majesty applies last-resort measures to scrutinize ordinary people—your servant believes this fails the principle of adapting to the times.

sentences.zh: 頃年以來，伏見諸方告密。

translations.literal: In recent years I have humbly observed secret denunciations from every quarter.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years I have observed secret denunciations arising everywhere.

sentences.zh: 囚累百千輩。

translations.literal: Prisoners accumulate by the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners have accumulated by the hundreds.

sentences.zh: 大抵所告，皆以揚州為名，及其窮竟，百無一實。

translations.literal: For the most part those denounced were all charged under the name of Yangzhou; when fully investigated, not one in a hundred proved true.
translations.idiomatic: For the most part the accused were charged with ties to Yangzhou, yet when cases were fully investigated, scarcely one in a hundred proved true.

sentences.zh: 陛下仁恕，又屈法容之，傍訐他事，亦為推劾。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, being benevolent and forgiving, again bent the law to pardon them, but side denunciations of other matters were still pursued and impeached.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, being benevolent and forgiving, would bend the law to spare them, yet side denunciations of other matters were still pursued and prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 遂使奸臣之党，快意相讎，睚眥之嫌，即稱有密。

translations.literal: Thus the factions of treacherous ministers gratified themselves in mutual revenge; a grudge the size of a mote in the eye was at once declared a secret denunciation.
translations.idiomatic: Thus factions of treacherous ministers gratified themselves in mutual vengeance; a trifling grudge was instantly reported as a secret accusation.

sentences.zh: 一人被告，百人滿獄。

translations.literal: When one person was accused, a hundred filled the prisons.
translations.idiomatic: When one person was accused, a hundred filled the prisons.

sentences.zh: 使者推捕，冠蓋如市。

translations.literal: Envoys pursued and arrested; caps and carriage covers crowded like a market.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing envoys swarmed the roads, officials' caps and carriage covers thick as a marketplace.

sentences.zh: 或謂陛下愛一人而害百人，天下喁喁，莫知寧所。

translations.literal: Some said Your Majesty loved one person yet harmed a hundred; the realm murmured in fear, not knowing where to find peace.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Your Majesty would spare one man yet harm a hundred; the realm murmured in fear, uncertain where safety lay.

sentences.zh: 臣聞自非聖人，不有外患，必有內憂，物理自然也。

translations.literal: I have heard that unless one is a sage, if there is no external calamity there must be internal anxiety—such is the natural order of things.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that short of being a sage, if there is no external threat there will be internal troubles—such is the way of things.

sentences.zh: 臣不敢以古遠言之，請指隋而說。

translations.literal: I dare not speak from remotest antiquity; allow me to point to the Sui and speak.
translations.idiomatic: I dare not speak from remotest antiquity; permit me to take the Sui as my example.

sentences.zh: 臣聞長老云：隋之末世，天下猶平。

translations.literal: I have heard elders say: in the final years of the Sui, the realm was still at peace.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard elders say that in the Sui dynasty's final years the realm was still at peace.

sentences.zh: 煬帝不恭，窮毒威武，厭居皇極，自總元戎，以百萬之師，觀兵遼海，天下始騷然矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang was irreverent, exhausting cruelty and martial power, weary of dwelling at the imperial apex; he personally commanded the main army, reviewed troops on the Liao coast with an army of a million, and the realm at last grew restive.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang was irreverent, exhausting all severity and martial force, weary of dwelling at the imperial summit; he personally assumed command of the main army and paraded a million troops on the Liao coast—and the realm at last grew restive.

sentences.zh: 遂使楊玄感挾不臣之勢，有大盜之心，欲因人謀，以竊皇業。

translations.literal: This enabled Yang Xuangan to wield a disloyal power, harbor the heart of a great bandit, and seek through others' scheming to seize the imperial enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: This enabled Yang Xuangan to wield disloyal power, harbor the heart of a great rebel, and seek through conspiracy to seize the throne.

sentences.zh: 及稱兵中夏，將據洛陽，哮寔之勢傾宇宙矣。

translations.literal: When he raised arms in the central plains and was about to seize Luoyang, the roaring power overturned the universe.
translations.idiomatic: When he raised arms in the central plains and was about to seize Luoyang, his roaring momentum seemed ready to overturn heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 然亂未逾月，而頭足異處。

translations.literal: Yet the rebellion had not passed a month before head and feet were in different places.
translations.idiomatic: Yet within a month of the rebellion his head and body lay in different places.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 天下之弊，未有土崩，蒸人之心，猶望樂業。

translations.literal: The realm's ills had not yet reached earth-crumbling collapse; the hearts of the common people still hoped to prosper in their work.
translations.idiomatic: The realm's sickness had not yet reached total collapse; the common people still hoped to live and work in peace.

sentences.zh: 煬帝不悟，暗忽人機。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang did not understand, darkly neglecting the people's disposition.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang failed to understand, blindly ignoring the mood of the people.

sentences.zh: 自以為元惡既誅，天下無巨猾也，皇極之任，可以刑罰理之。

translations.literal: He thought that since the chief villain had been executed there were no great scoundrels left in the realm, and that the burden of the imperial apex could be managed through punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He believed that once the chief villain was dead no great scoundrels remained, and that imperial rule could be maintained through punishment alone.

sentences.zh: 遂使兵部尚書樊子蓋專行屠戮，大窮黨與，海內豪士，無不罹殃。

translations.literal: Thereupon he had Fan Zigai, Minister of War, carry out slaughter exclusively, exhaustively pursuing associates; eminent men throughout the realm none escaped calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he had Fan Zigai, Minister of War, carry out wholesale slaughter and exhaustively pursue associates; eminent men throughout the realm none escaped ruin.

sentences.zh: 遂至殺人如麻，流血成澤，天下靡然思為亂矣。

translations.literal: It reached the point of killing people like hemp stalks and blood forming marshes; the realm as one turned to thoughts of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: It reached the point where men were killed like hemp stalks and blood formed marshes; the whole realm turned to thoughts of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 於是蕭銑、硃粲起于荊南，李密、竇建德亂于河北。

translations.literal: Then Xiao Xian and Zhu Can rose in southern Jing, Li Mi and Dou Jiande stirred disorder in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Then Xiao Xian and Zhu Can rose in southern Jing, and Li Mi and Dou Jiande stirred rebellion in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 四海雲搖，遂並起而亡隋族矣。

translations.literal: Within the four seas clouds swayed; they rose together and destroyed the house of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Turmoil swept the four seas; they rose together and destroyed the house of Sui.

sentences.zh: 豈不哀哉！

translations.literal: Is it not lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Is it not lamentable!

sentences.zh: 長老至今談之，委曲如是。

translations.literal: Elders speak of it to this day; the details were just so.
translations.idiomatic: Elders speak of it to this day in just these terms.

sentences.zh: 觀三代夏、殷興亡，已下至秦、漢、魏、晉理亂，莫不皆以毒刑而致敗壞也。

translations.literal: Observing the rise and fall of the Three Dynasties, Xia and Yin, down through Qin, Han, Wei, and Jin—their order and disorder—none failed to bring ruin through cruel punishments.
translations.idiomatic: From the rise and fall of the Three Dynasties through Xia and Yin down to Qin, Han, Wei, and Jin, none failed to bring ruin through cruel punishment.

sentences.zh: 夫大獄一起，不能無濫。

translations.literal: When great trials are launched, there cannot fail to be excess.
translations.idiomatic: When great trials are launched, abuse cannot be avoided.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 刀筆之吏，寡識大方，斷獄能者，名在急刻。

translations.literal: Clerk-officials who wield brush and knife know little of broad principle; those skilled at deciding cases are famed for harsh urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Petty clerk-officials know little of broader principle; those skilled at deciding cases win renown for harsh urgency.

sentences.zh: 文深網密，則共稱至公，爰及人主，亦謂其奉法。

translations.literal: When documents are deep and nets tight, all call it supreme fairness; extending even to the sovereign, they too deem it upholding the law.
translations.idiomatic: When legal language grows dense and snares tighten, all praise it as supreme fairness; even the sovereign deems it faithful to law.

sentences.zh: 於是利在殺人，害在平恕，故獄吏相誡，以殺為詞。

translations.literal: Thus profit lay in killing people and harm in leniency and forgiveness; therefore prison officers admonished one another with killing as their watchword.
translations.idiomatic: Thus profit lay in condemning men to death and harm in leniency; prison officers warned one another to speak always of execution.

sentences.zh: 非憎於人也，而利在己。

translations.literal: It was not hatred of people, but profit for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: It was not hatred of people, but profit for themselves.

sentences.zh: 故上以希人主之旨，以圖榮身之利。

translations.literal: Therefore above they hoped to match the sovereign's intent; below they sought profit for their own advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Above they sought to match the sovereign's intent; below they pursued personal advancement.

sentences.zh: 徇利既多，則不能無濫，濫及良善，則淫刑逞矣。

translations.literal: Once yielding to profit became widespread, abuse could not be avoided; when abuse reached the good and innocent, excessive punishment ran rampant.
translations.idiomatic: Once the pursuit of profit spread, abuse became inevitable; when the innocent were swept up, cruel punishment ran rampant.

sentences.zh: 夫人情莫不自愛其身，陛下以此察之，豈非無濫矣！

translations.literal: In human nature none fail to cherish their own bodies; if Your Majesty scrutinizes by this, is there not bound to be abuse!
translations.idiomatic: No one fails to cherish his own life; if Your Majesty governs through such scrutiny, can abuse be avoided?

sentences.zh: 冤人籲嗟，感傷和氣；

translations.literal: The wronged lament in outcry, wounding harmonious qi;
translations.idiomatic: The wronged cry out in lament, damaging harmonious qi;

sentences.zh: 和氣悖亂，群生癘疫；

translations.literal: when harmonious qi turns perverse and chaotic, epidemics afflict all living things;
translations.idiomatic: when harmonious qi turns perverse, pestilence afflicts all living things;

sentences.zh: 水旱隨之，則有凶年。

translations.literal: floods and drought follow, and there are famine years.
translations.idiomatic: floods and drought follow, bringing famine years.

sentences.zh: 人既失業，則禍亂之心怵然而生矣。

translations.literal: When people lose their livelihoods, the heart of calamity and disorder is suddenly aroused.
translations.idiomatic: When people lose their livelihoods, the heart of calamity and disorder stirs awake.

sentences.zh: 頃來亢陽愆候，雲而不雨，農夫釋耒，瞻望嗷嗷，豈不由陛下之有聖德而不降澤於人也？

translations.literal: Recently severe drought with abnormal signs brought clouds without rain; farmers put down their plows and looked up crying in hunger—is this not because, though Your Majesty has sage virtue, blessing has not been sent down upon the people?
translations.idiomatic: Recently drought brought clouds without rain; farmers laid down their plows and looked up in hunger—is this not because Heaven withholds its blessing despite Your Majesty's sage virtue?

sentences.zh: 儻旱遂過春，廢于時種，今年稼穡，必有損矣。

translations.literal: If the drought passes into spring and planting is missed at its season, this year's crops will surely suffer loss.
translations.idiomatic: If drought persists past spring and planting is missed, this year's harvest will surely suffer.

sentences.zh: 陛下可不敬承天意，以澤恤人？

translations.literal: Can Your Majesty not reverently receive Heaven's intent and show moistening compassion to the people?
translations.idiomatic: Should Your Majesty not reverently heed Heaven's intent and show compassion to the people?

sentences.zh: 臣聞古者明王重慎刑罰，蓋懼此也。

translations.literal: I have heard that in antiquity enlightened kings deeply weighed punishments—surely they feared this.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that enlightened kings of old weighed punishment carefully—surely they feared this.

sentences.zh: 《書》不雲乎，「與其殺不辜，寧失不經。

translations.literal: Does not the Documents say: "Better to err in irregularity than to execute the innocent"?
translations.idiomatic: Does not the Book of Documents say: "Better to err through irregular leniency than to execute the innocent"?

sentences.zh: 」陛下奈何以堂堂之聖，猶務強國之威。

translations.literal: " Your Majesty—how can one of such majestic sagehood still pursue the awe of a strong state?
translations.idiomatic: " How can Your Majesty, in such majestic sagehood, still pursue the awe of a strong state?

sentences.zh: 愚臣竊為陛下不取。

translations.literal: Your foolish minister privately holds that Your Majesty should not choose this course.
translations.idiomatic: Your humble servant privately believes Your Majesty should not choose this path.

sentences.zh: 且愚人安則樂生，危則思變。

translations.literal: Moreover, when fools are secure they delight in life; when endangered they think of change.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when ordinary people feel secure they delight in life; when endangered they think of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 故事有招禍，法有起奸。

translations.literal: Thus affairs can summon calamity, and laws can breed treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Thus policy can summon calamity, and law can breed treachery.

sentences.zh: 倘大獄未休，支黨日廣，天下疑惑，相恐無辜，人情之變，不可不察。

translations.literal: If great trials do not cease and their branches daily widen, the realm grows doubtful, innocents fear one another, and shifts in human sentiment cannot go unobserved.
translations.idiomatic: If great trials do not cease and their branches spread daily, the realm grows doubtful, innocents fear one another, and shifts in popular sentiment cannot go unobserved.

sentences.zh: 昔漢武帝時巫蠱獄起，江充行詐，作亂京師，至使太子奔走，兵交宮闕，無辜被害者以萬千數。

translations.literal: Formerly in Emperor Wu of Han's time the witchcraft trials arose; Jiang Chong practiced fraud, stirred rebellion in the capital, drove the crown prince to flight, and brought arms to clash at the palace gates—innocents harmed numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In the time of Emperor Wu of Han the witchcraft trials arose; Jiang Chong practiced fraud and stirred rebellion in the capital, driving the crown prince to flight and bringing arms to the palace gates—the innocent harmed numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 當時劉宗幾覆滅矣，賴武帝得壺關三老上書，幡然感悟，夷江充三族，餘獄不論，天下少以安耳。

translations.literal: At that time the house of Liu was nearly destroyed; fortunately Emperor Wu received the memorial of the Elder of Huguan Pass, turned abruptly in realization, exterminated Jiang Chong's clan to three degrees, and ceased pursuing the remaining cases—only then did the realm briefly find peace.
translations.idiomatic: The house of Liu was nearly destroyed; only when Emperor Wu received the memorial of the Elder of Huguan Pass, turned abruptly in realization, exterminated Jiang Chong's clan to three degrees, and ceased the remaining trials did the realm briefly find peace.

sentences.zh: 臣讀書至此，未嘗不為戾太子流涕也。

translations.literal: When I read to this point in books, I have never failed to weep for Prince Li.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I read to this point, I cannot help weeping for Crown Prince Li.

sentences.zh: 古人云：「前事不忘，後事之師。

translations.literal: The ancients said: "Do not forget past affairs; they are teachers for what follows."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: "Do not forget past affairs; they are teachers for what follows."

sentences.zh: 」伏願陛下念之。

translations.literal: " I humbly pray Your Majesty will bear this in mind.
translations.idiomatic: " I humbly pray Your Majesty will bear this in mind.

sentences.zh: 今臣不避湯鑊之罪，以螻蟻之命，輕觸宸嚴。

translations.literal: Now I do not shrink from the crime of the boiling cauldron, risking this ant's life to lightly touch imperial majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Now I do not shrink from the boiling cauldron, risking my insignificant life to touch Your Majesty's august presence.

sentences.zh: 臣非不惡死而貪生也，誠以負陛下恩遇，以微命蔽塞聰明，亦非敢欲陛下頓息嚴刑，望在恤刑耳。

translations.literal: It is not that I do not hate death and cling to life; truly I am bound by Your Majesty's gracious favor and would block your clear insight with my humble life—I do not dare ask Your Majesty to halt stern punishment at once; my hope is simply mercy in punishment.
translations.idiomatic: It is not that I cling to life and fear death; truly I am bound by Your Majesty's gracious favor and would block your clear judgment with my humble life—I do not ask you to halt stern punishment at once; I ask only for mercy in punishment.

sentences.zh: 乞與三事大夫，圖其可否。

translations.literal: I beg to consult with the Three Chief Ministers on whether this may be done.
translations.idiomatic: I beg leave to consult the Three Chief Ministers on whether this may be done.

sentences.zh: 夫往者不可諫，來者猶可追，無以臣微而忽其奏，天下幸甚。

translations.literal: What is past cannot be remonstrated against; what is coming may still be pursued—do not disregard this memorial because your minister is insignificant; the realm would be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: What is past cannot be changed; what is coming may still be set right—do not disregard this memorial because your servant is insignificant; the realm would be greatly fortunate.

sentences.zh: 疏奏不省。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but ignored.

sentences.zh: 時司刑少卿徐有功常駁酷吏所奏，每日與之廷爭得失，以雪冤濫，因此全濟者亦不可勝數，語在《有功傳》。

translations.literal: At that time Xu Yougong, Vice Minister of Justice, often rebutted what the harsh officials reported, daily disputing with them in court over right and wrong to clear wrongful abuse; those thereby fully saved were also beyond counting—the account is in the Biography of Yougong.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xu Yougong, Vice Minister of Justice, often rebutted reports from harsh officials, disputing daily with them in court to clear wrongful abuse; those thereby saved were beyond counting—see the Biography of Xu Yougong.

sentences.zh: 及俊臣、弘義等伏誅，刑獄稍息。

translations.literal: When Lai Junchen, Wang Hongyi, and others were executed, penal trials gradually subsided.
translations.idiomatic: After Lai Junchen, Wang Hongyi, and others were executed, penal trials gradually subsided.

sentences.zh: 前後宰相王及善、姚元崇、硃敬則等，皆言垂拱已來身死破家者，皆是枉濫，則天頗亦覺悟。

translations.literal: Successively the chief ministers Wang Jishan, Yao Yuanchong, Zhu Jingze, and others all said that since the Chuigong era those who died or lost their families had all been wrongfully abused; Empress Wu herself also came partly to realize it.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers including Wang Jishan, Yao Yuanchong, and Zhu Jingze said in succession that since the Chuigong era those who died or lost their families had all been wrongfully punished; Empress Wu herself came partly to realize it.

sentences.zh: 於是監察御史魏靖上言曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon the investigating censor Wei Jing submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Investigating Censor Wei Jing submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞國之綱紀，在乎生殺。

translations.literal: I have heard that the bonds of the state lie in life and death.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the bonds of the state lie in the power of life and death.

sentences.zh: 其周興、來俊臣、丘神勣、萬國俊、王弘義、侯思止、郭弘霸、李敬仁、彭先覺、王德壽、張知默者，即堯年四凶矣。

translations.literal: Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, Qiu Shenji, Wan Guojun, Wang Hongyi, Hou Sizhi, Guo Hongba, Li Jingren, Peng Xianjue, Wang Deshou, and Zhang Zhimò—these were the Four Evils of Yao's reign.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, Qiu Shenji, Wan Guojun, Wang Hongyi, Hou Sizhi, Guo Hongba, Li Jingren, Peng Xianjue, Wang Deshou, and Zhang Zhimò—these were the Four Evils of Yao's age.

sentences.zh: 恣騁愚暴，縱虐含毒，讎嫉在位，安忍朝臣，罪逐情加，刑隨意改。

translations.literal: They indulged foolish brutality, unleashed cruelty and stored poison, envied those in office, and cruelly endured court ministers; crimes followed feeling in severity, punishments changed at whim.
translations.idiomatic: They indulged brutal folly, unleashed cruelty and poison, envied those in power, and callously abused court ministers; guilt was inflated by whim and punishments altered at will.

sentences.zh: 當其時也，囚囹如市，朝廷以目。

translations.literal: In their time prisons were like markets, and the court communicated by eyes alone.
translations.idiomatic: In their time prisons teemed like marketplaces, and the court communicated only by glances.

sentences.zh: 既而素虛不昧，冤魂有托，行惡其報，禍淫可懲，具嚴天刑，以懲亂首。

translations.literal: Then the plain and empty was not obscured; wronged souls found refuge; evil acts met retribution, excess wickedness could be punished; Heaven's stern punishment was fully applied to chastise the leaders of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Then truth could not be obscured; wronged souls found justice; evil met retribution and excess wickedness was punished; Heaven's stern sentence fell upon the leaders of disorder.

sentences.zh: 竊見來俊臣身處極法者，以其羅織良善，屠陷忠賢，籍沒以勸將來，顯戮以謝天下。

translations.literal: I have observed that Lai Junchen suffered the utmost penalty because he had framed the good, slaughtered and entrapped the loyal and worthy, confiscated property to warn the future, and displayed execution to appease the realm.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that Lai Junchen suffered the utmost penalty for framing the innocent, destroying the loyal and worthy, confiscating property to warn the future, and displaying his execution to appease the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞之道路，上至聖主，傍洎貴臣，明明知有羅織之事矣，俊臣既死，推者獲功，胡元禮超遷，裴談顯授，中外稱慶，朝廷載安。

translations.literal: I have also heard along the roads that from the sage sovereign down to noble ministers all clearly knew there was framing; once Junchen was dead those who pursued the cases were rewarded—Hu Yuanli was rapidly promoted, Pei Tan conspicuously appointed—and within and without all rejoiced; the court was at peace.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard along the roads that from the sage sovereign down to noble ministers all clearly knew cases were fabricated; once Junchen was dead those who pursued the cases were rewarded—Hu Yuanli was rapidly promoted and Pei Tan conspicuously appointed—and court and country rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 破其黨者，即能賞不逾時；

translations.literal: Those who broke up their faction were rewarded without delay;
translations.idiomatic: Those who broke up their faction were rewarded without delay;

sentences.zh: 被其陷者，豈可淹之累歲。

translations.literal: yet those they had entrapped—how could they be detained for years?
translations.idiomatic: yet those they had entrapped—how could they be detained for years?

sentences.zh: 且稱反徒，須得反狀。

translations.literal: Moreover, when men are called rebels, proof of rebellion must be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when men are called rebels, proof of rebellion must be obtained.

sentences.zh: 惟據片辭，即請行刑，拷楚妄加，款答何限。

translations.literal: On a fragment of words alone execution was requested; torture was wantonly applied, and confessions—who could limit them?
translations.idiomatic: On a fragment of testimony alone execution was sought; torture was wantonly applied, and confessions poured forth without limit.

sentences.zh: 故徐有功以寬平而見忌，斛瑟羅以妓女而受拘，中外具知，枉直斯在，藉以為喻，其餘可詳。

translations.literal: Thus Xu Yougong was envied for leniency and fairness, and Husheluo was detained over a prostitute—all within and without knew where wrong and right lay; take these as examples, and the rest may be understood in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Xu Yougong was envied for leniency, and Husheluo was detained over a prostitute—all knew where wrong and right lay; these examples suffice, and the rest need no elaboration.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞之，郭弘霸自刺而唱快，萬國俊被遮而遽亡。

translations.literal: I have also heard that Guo Hongba stabbed himself while shouting in satisfaction, and Wan Guojun was intercepted and suddenly died.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that Guo Hongba stabbed himself while shouting in triumph, and Wan Guojun was intercepted and died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 霍獻可臨終，膝拳于項；

translations.literal: Huo Xianke at his end had his knees drawn up to his neck;
translations.idiomatic: Huo Xianke at his death had his knees drawn up to his neck;

sentences.zh: 李敬仁將死，舌至於臍。

translations.literal: Li Jingren about to die had his tongue reach to his navel.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jingren near death had his tongue extended to his navel.

sentences.zh: 皆眾鬼滿庭，群妖橫道，惟徵集應，若響隨聲。

translations.literal: All were cases of ghosts filling the courtyard and demons blocking the road, omens gathering in response like echo following sound.
translations.idiomatic: All were omens of ghosts filling the courtyard and demons warring in the streets, signs gathering in response like echo following sound.

sentences.zh: 備在人謠，不為虛說，伯有晝見，殆無以過。

translations.literal: They are fully recorded in popular song; this is no empty tale—the daytime apparition of Bo You scarcely surpasses them.
translations.idiomatic: They are fully recorded in popular rumor—no idle tale; Bo You's daytime apparition scarcely surpasses them.

sentences.zh: 此亦羅織之一據也。

translations.literal: This too is evidence of framing.
translations.idiomatic: This too is evidence of fabricated prosecutions.

sentences.zh: 臣以至愚，不識大體，儻使平反者數人，眾共詳覆來俊臣等所推大獄，庶鄧艾獲申於今日，孝婦不濫于昔時，恩渙一流，天下幸甚。

translations.literal: I, in utmost foolishness, do not comprehend the larger pattern; if several persons were appointed to review and reinvestigate the great trials pursued by Lai Junchen and others, perhaps Deng Ai would gain vindication today and the filial widow would not suffer wrongful abuse as in former times—grace flowing on one current, the realm would be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: I, in my utmost foolishness, do not grasp the larger pattern; if several reviewers were appointed to reinvestigate the great trials pursued by Lai Junchen and others, perhaps Deng Ai would be vindicated today and the filial widow would not suffer as in former times—grace would flow uniformly, and the realm would be greatly fortunate.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，制令錄來俊臣、丘神勣等所推鞫人身死籍沒者，令三司重推勘，有冤濫者，並皆雪免。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; an edict ordered recording those whom Lai Junchen, Qiu Shenji, and others had pursued in trial until death with property confiscated, and commanded the Three Offices to reinvestigate; those wrongfully abused were all cleared and pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, an edict ordered a record of those whom Lai Junchen, Qiu Shenji, and others had prosecuted to death with confiscated property, and commanded the Three Offices to reinvestigate; all who had been wrongfully punished were cleared and pardoned.

sentences.zh: 中宗神龍元年，制以故司僕少卿徐有功，執法平恕，追贈越州都督，特授一子官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong under Emperor Zhongzong, an edict because the late Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud Xu Yougong had administered law with fairness and leniency posthumously ennobled him as Regional Inspector of Yuezhou and specially granted one son an office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shenlong under Emperor Zhongzong, an edict posthumously ennobled the late Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud Xu Yougong as Regional Inspector of Yuezhou and specially granted one son an office, in recognition of his fair and lenient enforcement of the law.

sentences.zh: 又以丘神勣、來子珣、萬國俊、周興、來俊臣、魚承曄、王景昭、索元禮、傅遊藝、王弘義、張知默、裴籍、焦仁亶、侯思止、郭霸、李敬仁、皇甫文備、陳嘉言、劉光業、王德壽、王處貞、屈貞筠、鮑思恭二十三人，自垂拱已來並枉濫殺人，所有官爵，並令追奪。

translations.literal: Also the twenty-three men—Qiu Shenji, Laizi Xun, Wan Guojun, Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, Yu Chengye, Wang Jingzhao, Suo Yuanli, Fu Youyi, Wang Hongyi, Zhang Zhimò, Pei Ji, Jiao Renyi, Hou Sizhi, Guo Ba, Li Jingren, Huangfu Wenbei, Chen Jiayan, Liu Guangye, Wang Deshou, Wang Chuzhen, Qu Zhenyun, and Bao Sigong—from the Chuigong era onward had all wrongfully killed people; all their titles and ranks were ordered revoked.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also stripped titles and ranks from twenty-three men—from Qiu Shenji and Laizi Xun through Bao Sigong—who since the Chuigong era had wrongfully executed people.

sentences.zh: 天下稱慶。

translations.literal: The realm rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: The realm rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 時既改易，制盡依貞觀、永徽故事。

translations.literal: As the times had changed, edicts entirely followed the precedents of Zhenguan and Yonghui.
translations.idiomatic: As the dynasty changed hands, edicts entirely followed Zhenguan and Yonghui precedents.

sentences.zh: 敕中書令韋安石、禮部侍郎祝欽明、尚書右丞蘇瑰、兵部郎中狄光嗣等，刪定《垂拱格》後至神龍元年已來制敕，為《散頒格》七卷。

translations.literal: An edict charged Zhongshu Ling Wei Anshi, Libu Shilang Zhu Qinming, Shangshu Youcheng Su Gui, Bingbu Langzhong Di Guangsi, and others to revise edicts from after the Chuigong Code through the first year of Shenlong, forming the Dispersed Promulgation Code in seven scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: An edict charged Chief Minister Wei Anshi, Vice Minister of Rites Zhu Qinming, Vice Director of the Secretariat Su Gui, Bureau Director Di Guangsi, and others to compile edicts issued since the Chuigong Code through the first year of Shenlong into the Dispersed Promulgation Code in seven scrolls.

sentences.zh: 又刪補舊式，為二十卷，頒於天下。

translations.literal: They also revised and supplemented the old formulary into twenty scrolls and promulgated it throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: They also revised and supplemented the old administrative formulary into twenty scrolls and promulgated it throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 景雲初，睿宗又敕戶部尚書岑羲、中書侍郎陸象先、右散騎常侍徐堅、右司郎中唐紹、刑部員外郎邵知與、刪定官大理寺丞陳義海、右衛長史張處斌、大理評事張名播、左衛率府倉曹參軍羅思貞、刑部主事閻義顓凡十人，刪定格、式、律、令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingyun, Emperor Ruizong again charged Household Minister Cen Xi, Zhongshu Shilang Lu Xiangxian, You Sanqi Changshi Xu Jian, You Si Langzhong Tang Shao, Xingbu Yuanwailang Shao Zhiyu, and the ten revision officials including Dali Sicheng Chen Yihai, Youwei Changshi Zhang Chubin, Dali Pingshi Zhang Mingbo, Zuowei Shuaifu Cao Cao Canjun Luo Sizhen, and Xingbu Zhushi Yan Yizhuan to revise the codes, formulary, statutes, and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jingyun, Emperor Ruizong again charged ten officials—including Household Minister Cen Xi, Vice Director of the Secretariat Lu Xiangxian, Palace Officer Xu Jian, Bureau Director Tang Shao, Vice Bureau Director Shao Zhiyu, and revision officials Chen Yihai, Zhang Chubin, Zhang Mingbo, Luo Sizhen, and Yan Yizhuan—to revise the codes, formulary, statutes, and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 太極元年二月奏上，名為《太極格》。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Taiji it was submitted, named the Taiji Code.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Taiji it was submitted under the title Taiji Code.

sentences.zh: 開元初，玄宗敕黃門監盧懷慎、紫微侍郎兼刑部尚書李乂、紫微侍郎蘇頲、紫微舍人呂延祚、給事中魏奉古、大理評事高智靜、同州韓城縣丞侯郢璡、瀛州司法參軍閻義顓等，刪定格、式、令，至三年三月奏上，名為《開元格》。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, Emperor Xuanzong charged Huangmen Jian Lu Huaihan, Ziwei Shilang and concurrent Xingbu Shangshu Li Yi, Ziwei Shilang Su Ting, Ziwei Sheren Lü Yanzuo, Jishizhong Wei Fenggu, Dali Pingshi Gao Zhijing, Tongzhou Hancheng Xian Cheng Hou Yingjin, Yingzhou Sifa Canjun Yan Yizhuan, and others to revise the codes, formulary, and ordinances; in the third month of the third year it was submitted, named the Kaiyuan Code.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, Emperor Xuanzong charged officials including Lu Huaihan, Li Yi, Su Ting, Lü Yanzuo, Wei Fenggu, Gao Zhijing, Hou Yingjin, and Yan Yizhuan to revise the codes, formulary, and ordinances; in the third month of the third year it was submitted as the Kaiyuan Code.

sentences.zh: 六年，玄宗又敕吏部侍郎兼侍中宋璟、中書侍郎蘇頲、尚書左丞盧從願、吏部侍郎裴漼慕容珣、戶部侍郎楊滔、中書舍人劉令植、大理司直高智靜、幽州司功參軍侯郢璡等九人，刪定律、令、格、式，至七年三月奏上。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Emperor Xuanzong again charged nine persons including Libu Shilang and concurrent Shizhong Song Jing, Zhongshu Shilang Su Ting, Shangshu Zuocheng Lu Congyuan, Libu Shilang Pei Cui and Murong Xun, Hubu Shilang Yang Tao, Zhongshu Sheren Liu Lingzhi, Dali Sizhi Gao Zhijing, and Youzhou Sigong Canjun Hou Yingjin to revise statutes, ordinances, codes, and formulary; in the third month of the seventh year it was submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Emperor Xuanzong again charged nine officials including Song Jing, Su Ting, Lu Congyuan, Pei Cui, Murong Xun, Yang Tao, Liu Lingzhi, Gao Zhijing, and Hou Yingjin to revise statutes, ordinances, codes, and formulary; in the third month of the seventh year it was submitted.

sentences.zh: 律、令、式仍舊名，格曰《開元後格》。

translations.literal: Statutes, ordinances, and formulary kept their former names; the code was called the Post-Kaiyuan Code.
translations.idiomatic: The statutes, ordinances, and formulary kept their former names; the code was titled Post-Kaiyuan Code.

sentences.zh: 十九年，侍中裴光庭、中書令蕭嵩，又以格後制敕行用之後，頗與格文相違，於事非便，奏令所司刪撰《格後長行敕》六卷，頒於天下。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, Palace Attendant Pei Guangting and Chief Minister Xiao Song, noting that after post-code edicts were put into practice they often conflicted with the text of the code and were inconvenient in affairs, memorialized ordering the relevant offices to compile and revise the Post-Code Long-Applicable Edicts in six scrolls and promulgate them throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, Palace Attendant Pei Guangting and Chief Minister Xiao Song, noting that edicts issued after the code often conflicted with its text and proved impractical, memorialized that the relevant offices compile the Post-Code Long-Applicable Edicts in six scrolls and promulgate them throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，戶部尚書李林甫又受詔改修格令。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, Minister of Revenue Li Linpu again received an edict to revise the codes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, Minister of Revenue Li Linpu received another imperial order to revise the codes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 林甫遷中書令，乃與侍中牛仙客、御史中丞王敬從，與明法之官前左武衛胄曹參軍崔見、衛州司戶參軍直中書陳承信、酸棗尉直刑部俞元杞等，共加刪緝舊格、式、律、令及敕，總七千二十六條。

translations.literal: Linpu was transferred to Chief Minister of the Central Secretariat; then together with Palace Attendant Niu Xianke, Censor-in-Chief Wang Jingcong, and legal specialists including former Left Brave Guard Armory Clerk Cui Jian, Weizhou Registrar Chen Chengxin on detail assignment to the Central Secretariat, Suanzao District Captain Yu Yuanqi on detail assignment to the Ministry of Justice, and others, they jointly added deletions and collation to the old codes, formulary, statutes, ordinances, and edicts — 7,026 articles in total.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Linpu was appointed Chief Minister, he worked with Palace Attendant Niu Xianke, Censor-in-Chief Wang Jingcong, and legal specialists including former Left Brave Guard armory clerk Cui Jian, Weizhou registrar Chen Chengxin on detail assignment to the Central Secretariat, Suanzao district captain Yu Yuanqi on detail assignment to the Ministry of Justice, and others to revise, prune, and collate the existing codes, formulary, statutes, ordinances, and edicts — 7,026 articles in all.

sentences.zh: 其一千三百二十四條於事非要，並刪之。

translations.literal: Of these, 1,324 articles were not essential to affairs and were all deleted.
translations.idiomatic: Of these, 1,324 articles deemed nonessential were struck entirely.

sentences.zh: 二千一百八十條隨文損益，三千五百九十四條仍舊不改。

translations.literal: 2,180 articles were amended according to the text; 3,594 articles remained unchanged as before.
translations.idiomatic: 2,180 were amended as the text required; 3,594 were left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 總成律十二卷，《律疏》三十卷，《令》三十卷，《式》二十卷，《開元新格》十卷。

translations.literal: In total there were completed: Statutes in twelve scrolls, Statute Commentaries in thirty scrolls, Ordinances in thirty scrolls, Formulary in twenty scrolls, and New Kaiyuan Code in ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: The compilation totaled twelve scrolls of statutes, thirty scrolls of statute commentaries, thirty scrolls of ordinances, twenty scrolls of formulary, and ten scrolls of the New Kaiyuan Code.

sentences.zh: 又撰《格式律令事類》四十卷，以類相從，便於省覽。

translations.literal: They also compiled Categories of Codes, Formulary, Statutes, and Ordinances in forty scrolls, arranged by category for convenient review.
translations.idiomatic: They also compiled Categories of Codes, Formulary, Statutes, and Ordinances in forty scrolls, grouped by subject for ease of reference.

sentences.zh: 二十五年九月奏上，敕于尚書都省寫五十本，發使散於天下。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twenty-fifth year it was submitted; an edict ordered fifty copies written at the Directorate-General of the Imperial Secretariat and envoys dispatched to distribute them throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the twenty-fifth year it was submitted to the throne; the emperor ordered fifty copies made at the Directorate-General of the Imperial Secretariat and dispatched throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 其年刑部斷獄，天下死罪惟有五十八人。

translations.literal: That year the Ministry of Justice decided cases; throughout the realm there were only fifty-eight death sentences.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Ministry of Justice handed down verdicts nationwide — only fifty-eight capital sentences in all.

sentences.zh: 大理少卿徐嶠上言：大理獄院，由來相傳殺氣太盛，鳥雀不棲，至是有鵲巢其樹。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Review Xu Qiao submitted a memorial: The prison courtyard of the Court of Review, as tradition had it, carried such a heavy air of killing that birds would not roost — until then magpies nested in its trees.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Review Xu Qiao memorialized the throne: The Court of Review's prison yard had long been said to carry such a heavy air of death that birds would not settle there — yet now magpies had built nests in its trees.

sentences.zh: 於是百僚以幾至刑措，上表陳賀。

translations.literal: Thereupon the hundred officials, because punishments were nearly set aside altogether, submitted memorials offering congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The officials took this as a sign that capital punishment had nearly been abolished altogether, and submitted congratulatory memorials.

sentences.zh: 玄宗以宰相變理、法官平允之功，封仙客為邠國公，林甫為晉國公，刑部大理官共賜帛二千匹。

translations.literal: Xuanzong, on account of the chancellors' merit in transforming governance and the judges' fair and even work, enfeoffed Xianke as Duke of Bin and Linpu as Duke of Jin; officials of the Ministry of Justice and Court of Review together were granted two thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong, crediting his chancellors with reforming governance and his judges with delivering equitable verdicts, enfeoffed Niu Xianke as Duke of Bin and Li Linpu as Duke of Jin, and granted officials of the Ministry of Justice and Court of Review two thousand bolts of silk between them.

sentences.zh: 自明慶至先天六十年間，高宗寬仁，政歸宮閫。

translations.literal: From the Mingqing era through the sixty years leading to Xiantian, Emperor Gaozong was generous and humane, and government passed to the inner chambers.
translations.idiomatic: From the Mingqing era through the sixty years leading to Xiantian, Emperor Gaozong ruled with generosity and forbearance while power slipped to the inner court.

sentences.zh: 則天女主猜忌，果于殺戮，宗枝大臣，鍛于酷吏，至於移易宗社，幾亡李氏。

translations.literal: Empress Wu the female ruler was suspicious and decisive in killing; clansmen and great ministers were forged by cruel officials, to the point of shifting the altars of state and nearly extinguishing the House of Li.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu, once enthroned, ruled with suspicion and ruthless bloodshed. Princes and ministers were broken on the rack of her cruel henchmen, until the dynastic succession itself was nearly wrenched from the House of Li.

sentences.zh: 神龍之後，後族幹政，景雲繼立，歸妹怙權。

translations.literal: After Shenlong, the empress's clan meddled in government; Jingyun succeeded to the throne; Princess Taiping relied on power.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shenlong restoration, the empress's kin again grasped at power; when Emperor Ruizong took the throne in the Jingyun era, Princess Taiping clung to authority at his side.

sentences.zh: 開元之際，刑政賞罰，斷於宸極，四十餘年，可謂太平矣。

translations.literal: At the Kaiyuan juncture, punishment, government, and the dispensation of reward and punishment were decided at the imperial apex; for more than forty years it could be called great peace.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign, criminal law and the dispensation of reward and punishment rested solely with the emperor — forty years that could truly be called an age of peace.

sentences.zh: 及塚臣懷邪，邊將內侮，乘輿幸于巴、蜀，儲副立于朔方，曾未逾年，載收京邑，書契以來，未有克復宗社若斯之速也。

translations.literal: When chief ministers harbored wickedness and frontier generals turned against the court within, the imperial carriage journeyed to Ba-Shu, the heir apparent was established at Shuofang — within barely a year the capital was recovered; since the invention of writing, never had restoration of the altars of state been so swift.
translations.idiomatic: When treacherous ministers and mutinous frontier generals drove the emperor into exile in Ba-Shu and installed the crown prince at Shuofang, the capital was retaken within a single year — a recovery of the dynasty swifter than any recorded since writing began.

sentences.zh: 而兩京衣冠，多被脅從，至是相率待罪闕下。

translations.literal: Yet the gentry of the two capitals, many coerced into following the rebels, now came in succession to await judgment below the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: Yet many officials of both capitals, having been forced to submit to the rebels, now came in droves to the palace to await judgment.

sentences.zh: 而執事者務欲峻刑以取威，盡誅其族，以令天下。

translations.literal: Yet those in charge sought only harsh punishments to display authority, exterminating entire clans to awe the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The men in charge, however, were bent on imposing harsh sentences to intimidate — they would wipe out entire families to make an example of the realm.

sentences.zh: 議久不定，竟置三司使，以御史大夫兼京兆尹李峴、兵部侍郎呂諲、戶部侍郎兼御史中丞崔器、刑部侍郎兼御史中丞韓擇木、大理卿嚴向等五人為之。

translations.literal: Deliberation long unsettled; finally they established the Three Commissions envoys, appointing five persons: Chief Censor and concurrent Jingzhao Intendant Li Xian, Vice Minister of War Lu Shen, Vice Minister of Revenue and concurrent Censor-in-Chief Cui Qi, Vice Minister of Justice and concurrent Censor-in-Chief Han Zemu, and Chief Minister of Review Yan Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Debate dragged on unresolved until the court appointed five commissioners — Chief Censor and Jingzhao Intendant Li Xian, Vice Minister of War Lu Shen, Vice Minister of Revenue and Censor-in-Chief Cui Qi, Vice Minister of Justice and Censor-in-Chief Han Zemu, and Chief Minister of Review Yan Xiang — to serve as the Three Commissions.

sentences.zh: 初，西京文武官陸大鈞等陷賊來歸，崔器草儀，盡令免冠徒跣，撫膺號泣，以金吾府縣人吏圍之，於朝謝罪，收付大理京兆府獄系之。
