translations.literal: Initially, civil and military officials of the Western Capital such as Lu Dajun who had fallen into the rebels' hands and returned — Cui Qi drafted the protocol, ordering all to remove caps and go barefoot, beating their chests and wailing; Gold Guard and prefectural clerks surrounded them; at court they confessed their crimes; they were taken and imprisoned in the Review and Jingzhao prisons.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Western Capital officials such as Lu Dajun who had fallen into rebel hands returned to the loyal side, Cui Qi drew up a ritual requiring them to remove their caps, go barefoot, beat their breasts, and wail. Gold Guard and prefectural officers surrounded them as they confessed their crimes at court, then they were handed over to the prisons of the Court of Review and the Jingzhao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及陳希烈等大臣至者數百人，又令朝堂徒跣如初，令宰相苗晉卿、崔圓、李麟等百僚同視，以為棄辱，宣詔以責之。

translations.literal: When several hundred great ministers including Chen Xilie arrived, again they were ordered to go barefoot in the court hall as before; the chancellors Miao Jinqing, Cui Yuan, Li Lin, and the hundred officials were made to watch together; regarding it as abandonment and humiliation, an edict was proclaimed to rebuke them.
translations.idiomatic: When several hundred senior officials including Chen Xilie arrived, they were subjected to the same barefoot humiliation in the hall of audience while Chancellor Miao Jinqing, Cui Yuan, Li Lin, and the rest of the bureaucracy looked on. The court, regarding this as a disgraceful spectacle, issued an edict rebuking the commissioners.

sentences.zh: 朝廷又以負罪者眾，獄中不容，乃賜楊國忠宅鞫之。

translations.literal: The court, because the guilty were numerous and the prisons could not hold them, granted Yang Guozhong's residence for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Because so many stood accused and the prisons could not hold them all, the court assigned Yang Guozhong's former residence as the venue for interrogations.

sentences.zh: 器、諲多希旨深刻，而擇木無所是非，獨李峴力爭之，乃定所推之罪為六等，集百僚尚書省議之。

translations.literal: Cui Qi and Lu Shen mostly sought the ruler's intent and were severe; Han Zemu took no sides on right and wrong; only Li Xian argued forcefully; then they fixed the proposed crimes in six grades and gathered the hundred officials at the Ministry of Personnel to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qi and Lu Shen largely shaped their judgments to please the throne and pressed for harsh penalties; Han Zemu neither affirmed nor challenged their findings; only Li Xian fought back vigorously. They eventually ranked the proposed offenses in six grades and summoned the bureaucracy to the Ministry of Personnel for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 肅宗方用刑名，公卿但唯唯署名而已。

translations.literal: Suzong was then employing penal law; the high officials merely nodded assent and signed their names.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong was then governing through harsh penal law, and the senior officials merely murmured assent and affixed their signatures.

sentences.zh: 於是河南尹達奚珣等三十九人，以為罪重，與從共棄。

translations.literal: Thereupon thirty-nine persons including Henan Intendant Daxi Xun were deemed to have grave guilt and were condemned together with accomplices.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-nine officials including Henan Intendant Daxi Xun were deemed to have committed grave offenses and were condemned along with their accomplices.

sentences.zh: 珣等十一人，於子城西伏誅。

translations.literal: Eleven including Xun were executed by decapitation west of Zi Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven, including Xun, were executed west of Zi Gate.

sentences.zh: 陳希烈、張垍、郭納、獨孤朗等七人，於大理寺獄賜自盡。

translations.literal: Seven including Chen Xilie, Zhang Ya, Guo Na, and Dugu Lang were granted death by their own hand in the Court of Review prison.
translations.idiomatic: Seven — Chen Xilie, Zhang Ya, Guo Na, Dugu Lang, and others — were permitted to take their own lives in the Court of Review prison.

sentences.zh: 達奚摯、張岯、李有孚、劉子英、冉大華二十一人，於京兆府門決重杖死。

translations.literal: Twenty-one including Daxi Zhi, Zhang Pi, Li Youfu, Liu Ziying, and Ran Dahua were beaten to death with heavy sticks at the Jingzhao prefecture gate.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-one — Daxi Zhi, Zhang Pi, Li Youfu, Liu Ziying, Ran Dahua, and others — were beaten to death with heavy cudgels at the gate of the Jingzhao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大理卿張均引至獨柳樹下刑人處，免死配流合浦郡，而達奚珣、韋恆乃至腰斬。

translations.literal: Chief Minister of Review Zhang Jun was brought to the execution ground beneath the Lone Willow Tree, spared death and sentenced to exile to Hepu Commandery; yet Daxi Xun and Wei Heng were cut in two at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister of Review Zhang Jun was taken to the execution ground beneath the Lone Willow Tree, spared death, and banished to Hepu Commandery — but Daxi Xun and Wei Heng were cut in two at the waist.

sentences.zh: 先是，慶緒至相州，史思明、高秀岩等皆送款請命，肅宗各令復位，便領所管，至是懼不自安，各率其黨叛。

translations.literal: Previously, when Qingxu reached Xiangzhou, Shi Siming, Gao Xiuyan, and others all sent pledges of allegiance begging for mercy; Suzong had each restored to office and immediately put in charge of their commands — at this they feared and were not at ease, each leading their faction in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when An Qingxu had reached Xiangzhou, Shi Siming, Gao Xiuyan, and others had all submitted pledges of loyalty and begged for pardon; Emperor Suzong had restored each to office and left them in command of their troops. Now, fearing for their lives, they each led their followers in revolt.

sentences.zh: 其後三司用刑，連年不定，流貶相繼。

translations.literal: Afterward the Three Commissions applied punishments; for years nothing was settled; exile and demotion followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Three Commissions continued their prosecutions year after year without resolution, and a stream of exiles and demotions followed.

sentences.zh: 及王璵為相，素聞物議，請下詔自今已後，三司推勘未畢者，一切放免，大收人望。

translations.literal: When Wang Yu became chancellor, having long heard public criticism, he requested an edict that from now on all those whose Three Commissions investigations were not yet complete be entirely released — greatly winning popular regard.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yu became chancellor, responding to widespread public outrage, he persuaded the throne to decree that all pending Three Commissions cases be dismissed — a move that won him tremendous goodwill.

sentences.zh: 後蕭華拔魏州歸國，嘗話於朝云：「初河北官聞國家宣詔放陳希列等脅從官一切不問，各令復位，聞者悔歸國之晚，舉措自失。

translations.literal: Later Xiao Hua captured Weizhou and returned to the loyal side; he once spoke at court, saying: "At first when officials in Hebei heard the state proclaim an edict releasing coerced followers such as Chen Xilie and the rest, questioning nothing, each restored to office — those who heard regretted returning so late and lost composure in their actions.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after Xiao Hua recaptured Weizhou and rejoined the loyal cause, he told the court: "When officials in Hebei first heard the decree pardoning coerced followers such as Chen Xilie and restoring them to office, many regretted having delayed their return and grew uncertain in their conduct.

sentences.zh: 及後聞希烈等死，皆相賀得計，無敢歸者。

translations.literal: When later they heard Xilie and others had died, all congratulated one another on their calculated choice; none dared return.
translations.idiomatic: But when word came that Chen Xilie and the others had been executed, they congratulated one another on their shrewd hesitation — and none dared defect back.

sentences.zh: 於是河北將吏，人人益堅，大兵不解。」

translations.literal: Thus the generals and officials of Hebei, each person growing firmer; the great army could not be disbanded."
translations.idiomatic: The Hebei commanders and officials grew only more resolute, and the rebellion dragged on without end."

sentences.zh: 後有毛若虛、敬羽之流，皆深酷割剝，驟求權柄，殺人以逞刑，厚斂以資國。

translations.literal: Later there were men like Mao Ruoxu and Jing Yu — all deeply cruel in extortion, suddenly seeking power, killing people to display punishments, heavy levies to supply the state.
translations.idiomatic: Later came men such as Mao Ruoxu and Jing Yu — cruel extortionists who seized power overnight, killing to satisfy their appetite for punishment and squeezing the people to fill the treasury.

sentences.zh: 六七年間，大獄相繼，州縣之內，多是貶降人。

translations.literal: Within six or seven years, great cases followed one after another; within prefectures and districts, most were demoted and exiled persons.
translations.idiomatic: Over the next six or seven years great trials followed one after another, and the prefectures and districts swarmed with the exiled and demoted.

sentences.zh: 肅宗復聞三司多濫，嘗悔云：「朕為三司所誤，深恨之。

translations.literal: Suzong again heard the Three Commissions were largely excessive; he once regretted, saying: "We have been misled by the Three Commissions — We deeply resent it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong, learning how reckless the Three Commissions had become, once lamented: "I was deceived by the Three Commissions — the resentment runs deep.

sentences.zh: 」及彌留之際，以元載為相，乃詔天下流降人等一切放歸。

translations.literal: " At the moment of his final illness, with Yuan Zai as chancellor, an edict was issued that all exiled and demoted persons throughout the realm be entirely released and returned.
translations.idiomatic: " On his deathbed, with Yuan Zai as chancellor, he issued an edict ordering all exiles and demoted officials throughout the realm to be released and sent home.

sentences.zh: 代宗寶應元年，回紇與史朝義戰，勝，擒其將士妻子老幼四百八十人。

translations.literal: Daizong, first year of Baoying: the Uyghurs fought Shi Chaoyi and won, capturing 480 soldiers, wives, children, old and young.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Baoying era under Emperor Daizong, the Uyghurs defeated Shi Chaoyi in battle and captured four hundred eighty of his soldiers together with their wives, children, and elderly dependents.

sentences.zh: 上以婦人雖為賊家口，皆是良家子女，被賊逼略，惻然湣之，令萬年縣於勝業佛寺安置，給糧料。

translations.literal: The emperor, though the women were counted among the rebel households, all were daughters of good families forced by rebels — he was moved to pity and ordered Wanian County to house them at Shengye Buddhist Temple and provide rations.
translations.idiomatic: Though these women were counted among the rebel camp, the emperor recognized them as daughters of respectable families who had been seized by force. Moved to pity, he ordered Wanian County to shelter them at Shengye Temple and provide rations.

sentences.zh: 若有親屬認者，任還之；

translations.literal: If relatives came to claim them, they were free to take them back;
translations.idiomatic: If relatives came forward to claim them, they were free to take them home;

sentences.zh: 如無親族者，任其所適，仍給糧遞過。

translations.literal: If without kin, free to go where they would, still given grain for transit.
translations.idiomatic: Those without kin were free to go wherever they chose, with travel rations provided for the journey.

sentences.zh: 於是人情莫不感戴忻悅。

translations.literal: Thereupon among the people none failed to feel gratitude and joy.
translations.idiomatic: The populace responded with universal gratitude and joy.

sentences.zh: 大曆十四年六月一日，德宗禦丹鳳樓大赦。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year of Dali, first day of the sixth month: Dezong held a great amnesty at Danfeng Tower.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the sixth month in the fourteenth year of the Dali era, Emperor Dezong proclaimed a general amnesty from Danfeng Tower.

sentences.zh: 赦書節文：「律、令、格、式條目有未折衷者，委中書門下簡擇理識通明官共刪定。

translations.literal: Amnesty text: "Where articles of statutes, ordinances, codes, and formulary have not been harmonized, charge the Secretariat and Chancellery to select clear-minded officials jointly to revise and fix.
translations.idiomatic: The amnesty proclamation read: "Where provisions of the statutes, ordinances, codes, and formulary remain unresolved, the Secretariat and Chancellery shall select learned and clear-sighted officials to revise them jointly.

sentences.zh: 自至德已來制敕，或因人奏請，或臨事頒行，差互不同，使人疑惑，中書門下與刪定官詳決，取堪久長行用者，編入格條。

translations.literal: From Zhide onward, regulatory edicts — sometimes from individual petitions, sometimes promulgated on urgent affairs — differed inconsistently and caused doubt; the Secretariat, Chancellery, and revision officials shall examine and decide, taking what can long be applied and compiling into code articles.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts issued since the Zhide era — whether in response to petitions or promulgated ad hoc — conflict with one another and sow confusion. The Secretariat, Chancellery, and revising officials shall adjudicate them carefully and incorporate those suitable for permanent use into the code.

sentences.zh: 」三司使，准式以御史中丞、中書舍人、給事中各一人為之，每日於朝堂受詞，推勘處分。

translations.literal: " The Three Commissions envoys — per formulary one Censor-in-Chief, one Secretariat Drafter, and one Director of Scrutiny each — daily at the court hall receive petitions, investigate and dispose.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Commissions shall comprise one censor-in-chief, one secretariat drafter, and one director of scrutiny, as the formulary prescribes. Each day they shall receive petitions in the hall of audience and conduct investigations and dispositions."

sentences.zh: 建中二年，罷刪定格令使並三司使。

translations.literal: Second year of Jianzhong: abolished the Revision of Codes and Ordinances commissioners and the Three Commissions envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Jianzhong era, the commissioners for revising codes and ordinances and the Three Commissions were abolished.

sentences.zh: 先是，以中書門下充刪定格令使，又以給事中、中書舍人、御史中丞為三司使。

translations.literal: Previously, the Secretariat and Chancellery served as Revision commissioners; directors of scrutiny, secretariat drafters, and the censor-in-chief served as Three Commissions envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the Secretariat and Chancellery had served as the commissioners for revising codes and ordinances, while directors of scrutiny, secretariat drafters, and the censor-in-chief had staffed the Three Commissions.

sentences.zh: 至是中書門下奏請復舊，以刑部、御史臺、大理寺為之。

translations.literal: At this time the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized requesting restoration of the old arrangement — the Ministry of Justice, Censorate, and Court of Review to serve.
translations.idiomatic: At this point the Secretariat and Chancellery petitioned to restore the former arrangement, with the Ministry of Justice, Censorate, and Court of Review resuming responsibility.

sentences.zh: 其格令委刑部刪定。

translations.literal: The codes and ordinances were entrusted to the Ministry of Justice for revision.
translations.idiomatic: Revision of the codes and ordinances was assigned to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 元和四年九月敕：「刑部大理決斷系囚，過為淹遲，是長奸幸。

translations.literal: Fourth year of Yuanhe, ninth month edict: "The Ministry of Justice and Court of Review in deciding imprisoned persons are excessively delayed — this nurtures villainy and impunity.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of the ninth month of the fourth year of the Yuanhe era: "The Ministry of Justice and Court of Review take far too long to resolve cases involving prisoners — a delay that only encourages criminal impunity.

sentences.zh: 自今已後，大理寺檢斷，不得過二十日，刑部覆下，不得過十日。

translations.literal: From now on, Court of Review examination and decision shall not exceed twenty days; Ministry of Justice review and downward transmission shall not exceed ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the Court of Review's review and adjudication shall not exceed twenty days, and the Ministry of Justice's confirmation shall not exceed ten days.

sentences.zh: 如刑部覆有異同，寺司重加不得過十五日，省司量覆不得過本日。

translations.literal: If the Ministry's review differs, the Court's re-examination shall not exceed fifteen days; the Ministry's measured review shall not exceed that same day count.
translations.idiomatic: If the Ministry of Justice's review yields a discrepancy, the Court's re-examination shall not exceed fifteen days, and the Ministry's follow-up review shall observe the same deadline.

sentences.zh: 如有牒外州府節目及於京城內勘，本推即日以報。

translations.literal: If there are matters requiring dispatches to outer prefectures or investigation within the capital, the investigating office shall report the same day.
translations.idiomatic: When a case requires dispatch to an outer prefecture or investigation within the capital, the investigating office shall report its findings the same day.

sentences.zh: 牒到後計日數，被勘司卻報不得過五日。

translations.literal: After the dispatch arrives, counting days, the office under investigation's return report shall not exceed five days.
translations.idiomatic: Once a dispatch arrives, the office under investigation shall reply within five days.

sentences.zh: 仍令刑部具遣牒及報牒月日，牒報都省及分察使，各准敕文勾舉糾訪。」

translations.literal: Also order the Ministry of Justice to record dates of outgoing and returning dispatches; report to the Directorate-General and separate investigating envoys, each per edict text to check, raise, and investigate."
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice shall record the dates of all outgoing and returning dispatches and report them to the Directorate-General and the separate investigating commissioners, who shall monitor compliance and report any violations."

sentences.zh: 六年九月，富平縣人梁悅，為父殺仇人秦果，投縣請罪。

translations.literal: Sixth year, ninth month: Liang Yue of Fuping County killed his father's enemy Qin Guo, presented himself at the county to confess.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the sixth year, Liang Yue of Fuping County killed Qin Guo, his father's murderer, and turned himself in at the county magistrate's office to accept punishment.

sentences.zh: 敕：「復仇殺人，固有彝典。

translations.literal: Edict: "Revenge killing — there is indeed the constant canon.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Vengeance killing is subject to the eternal law.

sentences.zh: 以其申冤請罪，視死如歸，自詣公門，發於天性。

translations.literal: Because he declared his grievance and begged punishment, facing death as returning home, coming of himself to the public gate — arising from natural disposition.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this man came forward of his own accord to declare his grievance and accept judgment, facing death as one might a homecoming — an act born of primal filial instinct.

sentences.zh: 志在徇節，本無求生之心，寧失不經，特從減死之法。

translations.literal: His intent to follow righteousness; originally no mind to live; better err than miss — specially follow the reduced-death law.
translations.idiomatic: He sought only to fulfill his duty, with no thought of escape; rather than punish too lightly, We choose leniency — commuted from death under special grounds.

sentences.zh: 宜決一百，配流循州。

translations.literal: Should receive one hundred blows, banished to Xun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He shall receive one hundred strokes of the cudgel and be banished to Xun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 」職方員外郎韓愈獻議曰：

translations.literal: " Vice Director of the Office of Army Appointments Han Yu submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: " Vice Director of the Office of Army Appointments Han Yu submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 伏奉今月五日敕：復仇，據禮經則義不同天，征法令則殺人者死。

translations.literal: I humbly received this month's fifth-day edict: Revenge — according to the ritual classics, the obligation differs from Heaven; invoking the legal statutes, one who kills shall die.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully received the edict of the fifth of this month: on the question of revenge, the ritual classics hold that filial obligation is as weighty as Heaven itself, while the legal code declares that one who kills shall die.

sentences.zh: 禮法二事，皆王教之端，有此異同，必資論辯，宜令都省集議聞奏者。

translations.literal: Ritual and law are both foundations of royal teaching; with this difference and sameness, debate is surely required — it is fitting to order the Directorate-General to gather for deliberation and report.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual and law alike are the twin foundations of royal governance. Where they diverge, reasoned debate is essential — hence the order that the Directorate-General convene for deliberation and report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 伏以子復父仇，見於《春秋》，見於《禮記》，又見於《周官》，又見於諸子史，不可勝數，未有非而罪之者也。

translations.literal: I submit that a son avenging his father's enemy appears in the Spring and Autumn Annals, appears in the Book of Rites, also appears in the Rites of Zhou, also appears in the various masters and histories — too many to count — and never has one been condemned and punished for it.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that a son avenging his father's murder appears in the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Book of Rites, the Rites of Zhou, and countless other canonical and historical texts — and never once has such an act been condemned and punished.

sentences.zh: 最宜詳於律，而律無其條，非闕文也。

translations.literal: It is most fitting to be detailed in the statutes, yet the statutes have no such article — this is not a lacuna in the text.
translations.idiomatic: This matter ought to be addressed in the statutes, yet no such provision exists — and this is no accidental omission.

sentences.zh: 蓋以為不許復仇，則傷孝子之心，而乖先王之訓；

translations.literal: It is presumably because to forbid revenge would wound the heart of the filial son and violate the instruction of the former kings;
translations.idiomatic: The reason, I believe, is that forbidding revenge would wound the filial heart and betray the teaching of the ancient kings;

sentences.zh: 許復仇，則人將倚法專殺，無以禁止其端矣。

translations.literal: To permit revenge would mean people relying on the law to kill on their own authority, with no means to restrain the beginning of it.
translations.idiomatic: yet permitting it would invite people to take the law into their own hands, with no means to check the violence at its source.

sentences.zh: 夫律雖本于聖人，然執而行之者，有司也。

translations.literal: The statutes, though rooted in the sages, are yet enforced and carried out by the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: Though the statutes derive from the sages, it is the officials who enforce them.

sentences.zh: 經之所明者，制有司也。

translations.literal: What the classics make clear governs the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: What the classics illuminate is meant to guide those same officials.

sentences.zh: 丁甯其義於經，而深沒其文於律者，其意將使法吏一斷於法，而經術之士，得引經而議也。

translations.literal: Fixing its meaning in the classics yet deeply burying its text in the statutes — the intent is to make legal clerks decide entirely by statute, while scholars of the classics may cite the classics in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: By anchoring the principle in the classics while burying the matter deep in the statutes, the intent is to bind the legal clerks to the letter of the law while allowing scholars of the classics to invoke canonical authority in deliberation.

sentences.zh: 《周官》曰：「凡殺人而義者，令勿仇，仇之則死。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou says: "For all who kill a person justly, order that no revenge be taken; if revenge is taken, death.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou states: "When one kills another justly, forbid revenge upon him; whoever takes revenge shall die.

sentences.zh: 」義，宜也，明殺人而不得其宜者，子得復仇也。

translations.literal: " Righteousness means fitting; making clear that one who kills without fitting justification — a son may take revenge.
translations.idiomatic: " 'Righteous' means 'fitting.' This makes clear that when a man is killed without just cause, his son may take revenge.

sentences.zh: 此百姓之相仇者也。

translations.literal: This concerns common people taking revenge on one another.
translations.idiomatic: This concerns private blood feuds among common people.

sentences.zh: 《公羊傳》曰：「父不受誅，子復仇可也。

translations.literal: The Gongyang Commentary says: "If the father did not deserve execution, the son may take revenge.
translations.idiomatic: The Gongyang Commentary says: "If the father did not deserve execution, the son may take revenge.

sentences.zh: 」不受誅者，罪不當誅也。

translations.literal: " One who did not deserve execution — the crime did not warrant execution.
translations.idiomatic: " 'Did not deserve execution' means the crime did not warrant capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 又《周官》曰：「凡報仇讎者，書於士，殺之無罪。

translations.literal: Again the Rites of Zhou says: "For all who take revenge on an enemy, record it with the officer; killing is without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou also states: "Whoever seeks to take revenge must first register his intent with the magistrate; if he then kills his enemy, he is without guilt.

sentences.zh: 」言將復仇，必先言於官，則無罪也。

translations.literal: " Speaking of intending revenge, one must first speak to the official — then there is no guilt.
translations.idiomatic: " This means that one who intends revenge must first declare it to the authorities — only then is he without guilt.

sentences.zh: 今陛下垂意典章，思立定制。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty attends to the canon and statutes, thinking to establish fixed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty now attends to the canon of law, seeking to establish fixed regulations.

sentences.zh: 惜有司之守，憐孝子之心，示不自專，訪議群下。

translations.literal: Pitying the adherence of the relevant offices, sympathizing with the heart of the filial son, showing that you do not act on your own authority, consulting the deliberations of the assembled officials below.
translations.idiomatic: Out of regard for the strict adherence of officials to the letter of the law, and sympathy for the filial heart, you decline to decide alone and seek counsel from the assembled officials.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為復仇之名雖同，而其事各異。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks that though the name of revenge is the same, the affairs differ in each case.
translations.idiomatic: I am convinced that though all such acts bear the name of revenge, the circumstances differ in each case.

sentences.zh: 或百姓相仇，如《周官》所稱，可議於今者；

translations.literal: Some are common people taking revenge on one another, as the Rites of Zhou describes — these may be deliberated upon for the present;
translations.idiomatic: Some cases involve private blood feuds among common people, as described in the Rites of Zhou — these may be adjudicated under present law;

sentences.zh: 或為官吏所誅，如《公羊》所稱，不可行於今者。

translations.literal: Some are executed by officials, as the Gongyang describes — these cannot be applied in the present.
translations.idiomatic: others involve fathers executed by officials, as the Gongyang Commentary describes — a principle that cannot be applied today.

sentences.zh: 又《周官》所稱，將復仇，先告於士則無罪者。

translations.literal: Again, as the Rites of Zhou describes, one intending revenge who first reports to the officer is without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou also stipulates that one who registers his intent to take revenge with the magistrate before acting is without guilt.

sentences.zh: 若孤稚羸弱，抱微志而伺敵人之便，恐不能自言於官，未可以為斷於今也。

translations.literal: If one is orphaned, young, weak and frail, harboring a small resolve while waiting for the enemy's opportunity — fearing one cannot speak for oneself to the official — this cannot serve as a precedent for judgment in the present.
translations.idiomatic: But an orphaned youth, frail and alone, nursing a private vow while waiting for his enemy's moment of vulnerability, may well be unable to declare himself to the authorities — and this cannot serve as a precedent for judgment today.

sentences.zh: 然則殺之與赦，不可一例。

translations.literal: Thus execution and pardon cannot be treated by a single precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Execution and pardon, then, cannot be governed by a single rule.

sentences.zh: 宜定其制曰：凡有復父仇者，事發，具其事由，下尚書省集議奏聞。

translations.literal: It is fitting to fix a regulation saying: For all who avenge a father's enemy, when the matter arises, fully set forth the circumstances, send down to the Ministry of Personnel for collective deliberation and report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: I propose a regulation: whenever a man avenges his father's murder, the full circumstances shall be submitted to the Ministry of Personnel for collective deliberation and report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 酌其宜而處之，則經律無失其指矣。

translations.literal: Weigh what is fitting and dispose accordingly — then the classics and statutes will not lose their intent.
translations.idiomatic: Let each case be weighed on its merits — and neither the classics nor the statutes will lose their proper meaning.

sentences.zh: 元和十三年八月，鳳翔節度使鄭余慶等詳定《格後敕》三十卷，右司郎中崔郾等六人修上。

translations.literal: Thirteenth year of Yuanhe, eighth month: Military Commissioner of Fengxiang Zheng Yuqing and others thoroughly fixed the Post-Code Edicts in thirty scrolls; six persons including Right Department Director Cui Yan revised and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the thirteenth year of the Yuanhe era, Military Commissioner of Fengxiang Zheng Yuqing and others completed a thorough revision of the Post-Code Edicts in thirty scrolls, submitted by six revisers including Right Department Director Cui Yan.

sentences.zh: 其年，刑部侍郎許孟容、蔣乂等奉詔刪定，復勒成三十卷。

translations.literal: That year, Vice Ministers of Justice Xu Mengrong, Jiang Yi, and others received an edict to revise and fix them, again compiled into thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, Vice Ministers of Justice Xu Mengrong, Jiang Yi, and others were ordered to revise the compilation, producing a new edition of thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 刑部侍郎劉伯芻等考定，如其舊卷。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Justice Liu Bochu and others examined and fixed them, matching the former scroll count.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Justice Liu Bochu and others reviewed and ratified the work, preserving the original thirty-scroll format.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年五月，御史中丞牛僧孺奏：「天下刑獄，苦於淹滯，請立程限。

translations.literal: First year of Changqing, fifth month: Censor-in-Chief Niu Sengru memorialized: "Criminal cases throughout the realm suffer from delay and stagnation — I request that time limits be established.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of the Changqing era, Censor-in-Chief Niu Sengru memorialized: "Criminal cases throughout the realm languish in delay. I request that time limits be established.

sentences.zh: 大事，大理寺限三十五日詳斷畢，申刑部，限三十日聞奏。

translations.literal: Major cases: the Court of Review limited to thirty-five days for thorough decision completed, reported to the Ministry of Justice, limited to thirty days for report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: For major cases, the Court of Review shall complete its review within thirty-five days and report to the Ministry of Justice, which shall submit its findings to the throne within thirty days.

sentences.zh: 中事，大理寺三十日，刑部二十五日。

translations.literal: Medium cases: Court of Review thirty days, Ministry of Justice twenty-five days.
translations.idiomatic: For medium cases, the Court of Review shall have thirty days and the Ministry of Justice twenty-five.

sentences.zh: 小事，大理寺二十五日，刑部二十日。

translations.literal: Minor cases: Court of Review twenty-five days, Ministry of Justice twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: For minor cases, the Court of Review shall have twenty-five days and the Ministry of Justice twenty.

sentences.zh: 一狀所犯十人以上，所斷罪二十件以上，為大。

translations.literal: One case involving ten or more offenders, with twenty or more crimes adjudicated, counts as major.
translations.idiomatic: A case involving ten or more offenders and twenty or more adjudicated offenses shall be classified as major.

sentences.zh: 所犯六人以上，所斷罪十件以上，為中。

translations.literal: Six or more offenders, ten or more crimes adjudicated, counts as medium.
translations.idiomatic: Six or more offenders and ten or more adjudicated offenses shall be classified as medium.

sentences.zh: 所犯五人以下，所斷罪十件以下，為小。

translations.literal: Five or fewer offenders, ten or fewer crimes adjudicated, counts as minor.
translations.idiomatic: Five or fewer offenders and ten or fewer adjudicated offenses shall be classified as minor.

sentences.zh: 其或所抵罪狀並所結刑名並同者，則雖人數甚多，亦同一人之例。

translations.literal: If the offenses charged and the punishments fixed were all the same, then even if the number of persons was very great, they were treated by the precedent of a single person.
translations.idiomatic: When the offenses charged and the penalties imposed were identical, even a large number of offenders were counted as a single case.

sentences.zh: 違者罪有差。

translations.literal: Those who violated this had punishments of varying degree.
translations.idiomatic: Violations were punished according to degree.

sentences.zh: 」二年四月，刑部員外郎孫革奏：「京兆府雲陽縣人張蒞，欠羽林官騎康憲錢米。

translations.literal: " In the fourth month of the second year, Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice Sun Ge memorialized: "Zhang Li of Yunyang County in Jingzhao Prefecture owed money and grain to Kang Xian, an officer-rider of the Palace Guards."
translations.idiomatic: " In the fourth month of the second year, Vice Director Sun Ge of the Ministry of Justice memorialized: "Zhang Li of Yunyang County in Jingzhao owed money and grain to Kang Xian, an officer of the Palace Guards."

sentences.zh: 憲征之，蒞承醉拉憲，氣息將絕。

translations.literal: Xian pressed him for payment; Li, taking advantage of drunkenness, seized Xian, and his breath was nearly gone.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian pressed for payment, Li seized him while drunk and nearly strangled him.

sentences.zh: 憲男買得，年十四，將救其父。

translations.literal: Xian's son Maide was fourteen years old and was about to rescue his father.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's son Maide, aged fourteen, came to rescue his father.

sentences.zh: 以蒞角牴力人，不敢捴解，遂持木鍤擊蒞之首見血，後三日致死者。

translations.literal: Because Li butted with his head and struggled with great force, [Maide] did not dare grapple and release him, but took a wooden spade and struck Li on the head until blood appeared; three days later Li died.
translations.idiomatic: Li butted and struggled violently; Maide dared not grapple with him to pull him off, but struck Li on the head with a wooden spade until blood flowed. Li died three days later.

sentences.zh: 准律，父為人所毆，子往救，擊其人折傷，減凡鬥三等。

translations.literal: According to the statute, when a father is beaten by another and the son goes to rescue him and strikes that person so that bones are broken, ordinary assault is reduced by three grades.
translations.idiomatic: By statute, when a son rescues a father under assault and injures the assailant, the penalty for ordinary assault is reduced by three grades.

sentences.zh: 至死者，依常律。

translations.literal: If death results, the ordinary statute applies.
translations.idiomatic: If death results, the ordinary statute applies.

sentences.zh: 即買得救父難是性孝，非暴；

translations.literal: Thus Maide's rescuing his father in difficulty was filial nature, not violence;
translations.idiomatic: Maide's rescue of his father sprang from filial nature, not violence;

sentences.zh: 擊張蒞是心切，非凶。

translations.literal: striking Zhang Li was heartfelt urgency, not ferocity.
translations.idiomatic: his striking Zhang Li arose from urgent devotion, not ferocity.

sentences.zh: 以髫丱之歲，正父子之親，若非聖化所加，童子安能及此？

translations.literal: At the age of childhood tresses, in the fullness of father-son affection—if not for the sage transformation applied, how could a boy reach this?
translations.idiomatic: At such a tender age, in the fullness of father-son devotion—without the sage influence of your reign, how could a child achieve such a deed?

sentences.zh: 《王制》稱五刑之理，必原父子之親以權之，慎測淺深之量以別之。

translations.literal: The Royal Regulations say that the principle of the five punishments must take father-son affection as the weight in deliberation and carefully measure the degrees of lightness and depth to distinguish them.
translations.idiomatic: The Royal Regulations state that the principle of the five punishments must weigh father-son affection and carefully measure degrees of severity.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》之義，原心定罪。

translations.literal: The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals is to examine the heart in fixing guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals teach that guilt is determined by examining the heart.

sentences.zh: 周書所訓，諸罰有權。

translations.literal: What the Book of Zhou instructs is that all punishments have discretionary latitude.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Zhou instructs that all punishments allow discretionary latitude.

sentences.zh: 今買得生被皇風，幼符至孝，哀矜之宥，伏在聖慈。

translations.literal: Now Maide has received the imperial wind from birth; in youth he conforms to utmost filial piety—compassionate pardon lies humbly in sage compassion.
translations.idiomatic: Maide has lived under your sage influence from birth and in youth has shown utmost filial devotion. Compassionate pardon rests in your mercy alone.

sentences.zh: 臣職當讞刑，合分善惡。

translations.literal: Your servant's duty is to deliberate on punishments; it is fitting to distinguish good and evil.
translations.idiomatic: It is my duty to deliberate on punishments and to distinguish right from wrong.

sentences.zh: 」敕：「康買得尚在童年，能知子道，雖殺人當死，而為父可哀。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "Kang Maide is still in childhood and understands the way of the son; though killing a man deserves death, acting for his father is pitiable."
translations.idiomatic: " An edict declared: "Kang Maide is still a child and understands a son's duty. Though killing a man warrants death, his act on his father's behalf is deeply pitiable."

sentences.zh: 若從沉命之科，恐失原情之義，宜付法司，減死罪一等。」

translations.literal: If one follows the category of sinking life, I fear the meaning of examining feeling will be lost; he should be handed to the legal offices and the death penalty reduced by one grade."
translations.idiomatic: To apply the full penalty for homicide would lose the principle of weighing intent. Hand the case to the judicial offices and reduce the death penalty by one grade."

sentences.zh: 大和七年十二月，刑部奏：「先奉敕詳定前大理丞謝登《新編格後敕》六十卷者。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the seventh year of Dahe, the Ministry of Justice memorialized: "We were earlier ordered to examine in detail the sixty scrolls of Newly Compiled Regulations and Subsequent Edicts by former Assistant Grand Judge Xie Deng."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the seventh year of Dahe the Ministry of Justice memorialized: "We were earlier ordered to review the sixty scrolls of Newly Compiled Regulations and Subsequent Edicts submitted by former Assistant Grand Judge Xie Deng."

sentences.zh: 臣等據謝登所進，詳諸理例，參以格式，或事非久要，恩出一時，或前後差殊，或書寫錯誤，並已落下及改正訖。

translations.literal: Your servants, based on what Deng submitted, examined all principles and precedents and compared them with regulations and forms; some matters were not of lasting importance, favors issued for a moment; some differed before and after, or had errors in writing—all have been struck down or corrected and finished.
translations.idiomatic: We examined Deng's submission against principles, precedents, regulations, and forms. Provisions of passing importance, temporary favors, inconsistencies, and copying errors have all been struck or corrected.

sentences.zh: 去繁舉要，列司分門，都為五十卷。

translations.literal: Removing complexity and selecting essentials, arranging bureaus by category, in all fifty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Complexity was removed and essentials retained, organized by bureau and category, in fifty scrolls altogether.

sentences.zh: 伏請宣下施行。

translations.literal: We humbly pray that it be promulgated and put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly request that it be promulgated and put into effect.

sentences.zh: 」可之。

translations.literal: " Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 八年四月，詔應犯輕罪人，除情狀巨蠹，法所難原者，其他過誤罪愆，及尋常公事違犯，不得鞭背。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year, an edict said that for those who should commit light offenses—apart from circumstances of great corruption that the law cannot pardon—other errors, offenses, and faults, and ordinary violations of official business, flogging on the back was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the eighth year an edict declared that light offenders—apart from grave corruption that the law cannot pardon—were not to be flogged on the back for ordinary errors or routine violations of official duty.

sentences.zh: 遵太宗之故事也。

translations.literal: This followed the precedent of Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: This followed a precedent of Taizong.

sentences.zh: 俄而京兆尹韋長奏：「京師浩穰，奸豪所聚。

translations.literal: Before long Jingzhao Intendant Wei Chang memorialized: "The capital is vast and crowded, a gathering place for crafty and powerful men."
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jingzhao Intendant Wei Chang memorialized: "The capital is vast and crowded, a gathering place for the crafty and powerful."

sentences.zh: 終日懲罰，抵犯猶多，小有寬容，即難禁戢。

translations.literal: Punishment all day long, yet offenders remain numerous; a little leniency and they are hard to restrain.
translations.idiomatic: Despite constant punishment offenders remain numerous; the slightest leniency makes them hard to restrain.

sentences.zh: 若恭守敕旨，則無以肅清；

translations.literal: If I respectfully obey the edict, there is no means to bring order;
translations.idiomatic: If I strictly obey the edict, I cannot maintain order;

sentences.zh: 若臨事用刑，則有違詔使。

translations.literal: if in handling affairs I apply punishments, then I violate the edict and commission.
translations.idiomatic: if I apply punishments as circumstances require, I violate the imperial order.

sentences.zh: 伏望許依前據輕重處置。

translations.literal: I humbly hope permission to dispose according to lightness and heaviness as before.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly request permission to dispose of cases according to severity as before.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " [The request] was followed.
translations.idiomatic: " The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 開成四年，兩省詳定《刑法格》一十卷，敕令施行。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaicheng, the two departments examined and fixed the Criminal Law Regulations in ten scrolls; an edict ordered their implementation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaicheng the Secretariat and Chancellery completed the Criminal Law Regulations in ten scrolls, and an edict ordered their implementation.
